# Intake brief — Cards should represent the actual income and reputation changes

## Problem statement

During play, the income and reputation figures shown on a placed business or community-space card are derived from the card's static values plus any upgrade bonus (`baseIncome + incomeBonus` and `reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`). They ignore the modifiers the engine actually credits — board synergy, the same-type adjacency penalty, the duplicate-business (market-saturation) factor, and staff bonuses. A card can therefore display `+161` while the player is credited a different amount, so the card text contradicts the game economy and misleads placement and staffing decisions.

## Users

- **Players** who plan placements, upgrades and staff hires from the numbers shown on their cards.
  - "As a player, I want a placed card's text to show the income and reputation it actually generates, so I can make placement and staffing decisions without guessing."
  - "As a player, when I place a synergy neighbour or employ a Chef, I want the card's numbers to update immediately, so I can see the effect of my decision."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Placed business/community-space cards show the **effective per-turn income total** (base + upgrade bonus + synergy + duplicate factor + staff bonuses) in the on-card cash line, equal to the per-slot amount the engine credits.
- Placed cards show the **effective per-turn reputation total** (base + upgrade bonus + synergy) in the on-card reputation text, equal to the engine's per-slot reputation credit.
- Hover tooltips for placed street cards, hand cards and market cards show the same effective totals **and break them down** into base plus each modifier (upgrade, synergy, duplicate factor, staff), so no display surface shows stale base-only figures for a placed card.
- Every instance of a card, wherever it is displayed (a street slot, the hand, the market or any future surface), shows the modified income and reputation — never base-only figures — on the card face and in every hover tooltip.
- Staff bonuses are included in the displayed values on demand (read-only) without mutating the `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caches, reusing the same computation path as `applyIncome` so the displayed text can never disagree with the credited amount.
- Tests cover a plain card, a card with a synergy neighbour, a card with an employed staff bonus (own and adjacent), and a duplicate-saturated card, asserting the on-card total and the tooltip breakdown equal the engine's per-slot credited amounts.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players will be able to trust the income and reputation numbers on their cards: the card shows the coins and reputation actually credited each turn, and the tooltip explains how that total is built, so placement and staffing decisions are informed by real values rather than static base figures.

## Constraints

- The adjacency caches (`currentIncome`, `currentReputationPerTurn`) are read-only during display; staff buffs must be recomputed on demand, per the caching-safety contract documented in `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`.
- Display computation must share the engine's source of truth (`computeBusinessIncome`, `computeBusinessStaffBuffs`, `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`) so display and credit can never diverge.
- Rendering runs per card per refresh, so avoid expensive recomputation beyond what the engine already does each turn; memoise or cache per-slot effective values if needed.
- Baked SVG card faces (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and the static assets) currently show no income/reputation text; the fix is in the Phaser overlay/tooltip layer, not the SVG faces.
- Reduced-motion, replay and headless modes must remain visually and behaviourally unchanged.

## Existing state

- **On-card income/reputation:** `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`) computes `totalIncome = baseIncome + incomeBonus` and `totalReputation = reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`. These are rendered by `applyUpgradeOverlays()` on street, hand and market cards.
- **Street hover tooltip:** built inline in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` as `Income: +${baseIncome + incomeBonus}/turn`, with reputation from `reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`.
- **Hand/market hover tooltip:** `buildCardTooltipInfo()` in `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` uses the same base + bonus formula.
- **Actual values:** `card.currentIncome` = base + upgrade + synergy + duplicate factor (set by `syncCardCurrentIncome` / `recalculateCard` in `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`); `card.currentReputationPerTurn` = base reputation + upgrade bonus + synergy reputation. Staff buffs are deliberately **not** cached and are applied read-only in `applyIncome()` via `computeBusinessStaffBuffs()` and `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs()`.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg()` also uses base + bonus but is test-only (not on the production render path).

## Desired change

Make every card display surface show the modified values for that card instance wherever it appears: the card face shows the effective **total**, and the tooltip shows the total plus a **base + modifier breakdown**. Staff bonuses are included on demand, there is no location-based exception (hand, market and street instances all show modified values), and the adjacency caches are left untouched.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — accept/extract effective income and reputation totals (needs grid/staff context or precomputed per-slot values).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — pass per-slot effective values into the overlay spec and update the street tooltip text with the breakdown.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo()` (and any street tooltip builder) use effective totals plus the base/modifier breakdown for placed cards.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — expose a read-only per-slot effective income/reputation helper (total plus base/modifier components) reusing `computeBusinessIncome`, `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` and `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — existing staff buff helpers (consumed read-only; never mutated).
- `src/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `getIncomeResult()` preview path, if it should also agree with the effective values.
- `tests/main-street/` — new/updated tests asserting on-card totals and tooltip breakdowns equal the engine's per-slot credited amounts.

## Related work

- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** – Reputation bonuses should have no delay between businesses (completed).
- **MS-0MVRDGNFU001DDQW** – Park should give a good reputation bonus (completed).
- **MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y** – AI should not use Community Favour as much (completed).
- **MS-0MW0UCMF9004H9NT** – Single-player income: duplicate-factor applied to `computeBusinessIncome` / `syncCardCurrentIncome` (completed) — establishes the cached `currentIncome` values this item should display.
- **MS-0MVYG50V1007W8BP** – Reduced income for duplicate businesses (completed) — the duplicate-factor link surface.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "card text" means the on-card income/reputation overlay plus the hover tooltip. The baked SVG face shows no income/reputation today, so it is out of scope.
- **Confirmed (producer):** both surfaces are in scope; the card shows the effective total and the tooltip shows the breakdown into base and modifiers; staff bonuses are included.
- **Confirmed (producer, plan session):** *all* instances of a card, regardless of location (street, hand, market), show the modified data in both the card face and the tooltip — there is no unplaced-card exception.
- **Risk:** duplicating the income computation could drift from `applyIncome`; mitigate by extracting one shared read-only per-slot helper that returns both the total and its components.
- **Risk:** recomputing staff buffs per render could cost performance on large streets; mitigate with per-slot memoisation keyed on the turn/state revision.
- **Scope creep:** showing animated deltas on each card as bonuses change is a separate enhancement; record as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which surfaces must be in scope — the on-card overlay text, the hover tooltips, or both? — **Answer (producer):** Both; the tooltip breaks the value down into base and modifiers. Source: interactive reply. **Recommended option:** both, so the card and its tooltip never contradict each other.
- **Q:** Should the displayed income include staff bonuses (on-demand) or only the cached adjacency/synergy/duplicate effects? — **Answer (producer):** Include staff bonuses. Source: interactive reply. **Recommended option:** include staff bonuses, so the text matches the income actually credited.
- **Q:** Should the card show only the effective total, or also a breakdown of base / synergy / staff contributions? — **Answer (producer):** The card shows the total; the tooltip shows the breakdown. Source: interactive reply. **Recommended option:** effective total on the card, with the breakdown in the tooltip.

### Plan session (2026-11-08)

- Q: How should we reconcile parent AC3 ("hover tooltips for placed street cards, hand cards and market cards") with AC4 ("unplaced cards continue to show base + upgrade")?
  A (producer, plan session): "All instance of a card, regardless of their location in the game, should include the modified data in both the card and the tooltip." There is no unplaced-card exception.
  Final: **producer answer supersedes the earlier conservative reading.** AC4 rewritten to require modified values for every card instance wherever displayed; the overlay, tooltip, helper and integration-test children were revised to match.
- Q: None further — the intake appendix already resolved the scope decisions (both surfaces in scope, staff bonuses included, effective total on the card, breakdown in the tooltip).
  Final: intake answers stand unchanged.

## Plan

Six child tasks, test-first order:

1. **MS-0MW84013K0020ACZ** — Test: effective income/reputation helper returns correct totals and components
2. **MS-0MW84ALYG0065AWM** — Implement: read-only effective income/reputation helper with component breakdown
3. **MS-0MW843ARF0060F2K** — Implement: wire effective totals into card overlay spec
4. **MS-0MW843BSS0020R1B** — Implement: wire effective totals and breakdown into tooltips
5. **MS-0MW843CTF001WOCH** — Tests: on-card overlay and tooltip integration tests
6. **MS-0MW843DQQ00132PD** — Documentation: update code comments and docs

**Revision (producer clarification):** every card instance, in any location, shows the modified data on both the card and the tooltip. The former "unplaced cards keep base + upgrade" rule is retired, and children 1–6 were rewritten accordingly.

**Documented assumption for the no-slot case:** a hand or market instance has no board position, so position-dependent modifiers (adjacency synergy, same-type adjacency penalty, slot-bound staff buffs) evaluate to zero, while the upgrade bonus and the duplicate/saturation factor for its business type still apply — all resolved through the same shared helper, never a second formula. The instance is not counted twice when deriving its own saturation factor.
data.title: Cards should represent the actual income and reputation changes

# Assistant — verify documented staff effect (staff-assistant)

## Goal
Confirm that `staff-assistant` (Assistant, management-company) is properly defined — card data, parsed typed field, description text and docs — and that it behaves exactly as documented, by adding or tightening a behavioural test that asserts its documented effect and scope. This card is one of 26 per-card verification children under the parent audit epic `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND`.

## Documented effect (authoritative: GDD Appendix D.4)

- **Ability:** +2 hand slots
- **Scope:** player hand capacity (street-wide)
- **Backing data:** handSlotsAdded=2
- **Engine consumer:** maxHandSize (WeekStart / AiStrategy)
- **Existing behavioural test file:** `tests/main-street/MainStreetStaffCards.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Definition verified.** `staff-assistant` in `src/card-data.csv` carries the documented backing data (handSlotsAdded=2), the `description` text states the same effect at the same magnitude using the ×100 consistency rule, and `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` agree.

# Loan payoff dialog: carry the payoff across the competitive bailout pause

discovered-from:MS-0MW4887R4007XPGJ

## Goal (user story)

As a player in competitive play whose seat accepts a bankruptcy bailout offer
after its loan retired in the same closing, I want to still see the debt-free
congratulation once the day resumes, so that no payoff goes unnotified.

## Context

`MS-0MW4887R4007XPGJ` fixes the same class of gap on the single-player turn flow
(event-choice pause and bailout pause). The competitive FAQ tail has the
matching defect:

- `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`)
  returns into the loan-offer dialog when the closing pauses on
  `pendingLoanOffer`.
- The resume path calls `resolveCompetitiveLoanOffer(state, closing)`, which
  re-runs the closing with `skipLoanRepayments: true` — the repayments (and so
  the `loanPayoffs` report) already happened in the paused closing and are not
  re-reported. The resumed result therefore carries no payoffs, and the payoff
  sequencer (`presentLoanPayoffDialogs`) never presents the human seat's
  congratulation for an accepted offer.

## Desired change

Carry the paused competitive closing's `loanPayoffs` into the resumed tail and
present them through the existing `presentLoanPayoffDialogs` sequencer on the
continuing path only — never when the decline ends the run (game over wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play, a bailout-paused closing where the human seat accepts
   an offer presents exactly one congratulation when the day resumes, and
   never two.
2. A declined offer (the run ends) presents the game-over overlay and no
   congratulation.
3. The dialog appears only after the competitive closing presentation and never
   alongside another modal.
4. Unit tests cover the competitive pause/resume path, including the
   no-duplicate rule.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — carry the payoffs
  across the offer pause and present them in `presentCompetitiveDayTail`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveLoanOffer`
  (report the paused closing's retirements on the resumed result).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.ts` — `presentLoanPayoffDialogs`
  (reused unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/loan-payoff-turn-flow.test.ts` — competitive pause/resume
  cases.

## Constraints

- Presentation only: no engine arithmetic, wallet or RNG change.
- One modal at a time; the competitive pacing is unchanged.

## Implementation notes (plan review)

- **The paused closing already carries the report.**
  `finishCompetitiveClosingTail` (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`)
  returns both `pendingLoanOffer` pauses through `withLoanPayoffs`, and both
  happen *after* the `applyLoanRepayments` pass — so the closing handed to
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` already carries this day's retirements. No
  arithmetic, wallet or RNG change is needed.
- **The resumed closing loses it.** `resolveCompetitiveLoanOffer` re-runs only
  the failure/end-check tail with `skipLoanRepayments: true`, so the resumed
  result carries an empty `loanPayoffs`. Carry the paused closing's list across
  that seam in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (stash on the scene when the offer
  pauses, consume on resume), mirroring the `pendingBankingHint` carry the
  single-player flow uses in `MS-0MW4887R4007XPGJ`.
- **Pre-income pause is not affected.** The defensive `InvestmentResolution`
  pause resolves through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`, i.e. *before* the
  repayment pass, so its paused result has no `loanPayoffs` and the resumed
  re-run reports them normally — the carry is a no-op there, never a double
  report.
- **Presentation slot already exists.** `presentCompetitiveDayTail` calls
  `presentLoanPayoffDialogs(tcCtx.scene, closing.loanPayoffs, afterClosing)`
  inside the `presentCompetitiveClosing` completion callback, after the closing
  presentation and inside the Turn Summary gate — feeding it the carried list
  keeps one modal at a time (AC3).
- **Decline is already excluded.** The tail returns at
  `state.gameResult !== 'playing'` before that slot, and `shouldPresentLoanPayoff`
  additionally suppresses a run that is no longer `playing`, so game over wins
  (AC2).
- **No duplicate (AC1).** The paused pass never reaches the slot, so the resume
  is the only delivery; clear the carry once presented so a re-entry (double
  callback, F5 piggyback continuation) cannot replay it.
- **Test first.** Extend `tests/main-street/loan-payoff-turn-flow.test.ts`
  with the real competitive pause → resume flow (accept continues and presents
  exactly one dialog; decline ends the run and presents none). The file already
  pins "presents nothing before a pause and exactly one dialog for the resumed
  closing" with a hand-built result — extend it, do not duplicate that rule.


## Impact

A competitive player who accepts a bankruptcy bailout after their loan retired in the same closing now sees the debt-free congratulation once the day resumes — no payoff goes unnotified, and a declined offer still ends the run without one.

# Player hired staff, staff went to an AI business

**Score:** 0
**Rank:** new item (no parent)
**Type:** bug — **Pri:** critical

## Problem statement

In competitive play the street grid is shared and owner-tagged, but the staff employment paths never consult slot ownership: a walk-on staff applicant can be targeted at (and hired into) an AI opponent's business, and staff relocation can also move a player's member onto an opponent's business. The player pays the salary while the opponent's business gains the staff buff — the player's own hire silently strengthens a competitor.

## Users

- **Human player in competitive mode** — hires a walk-on staff applicant (or relocates a member) and expects the member to work *their* business.
  - As a competitive player, when a walk-on applicant appears I want them to walk into one of **my** businesses with a free employment slot, so that hiring them benefits me.
  - As a competitive player, when I relocate a staff member I want only my own businesses offered as destinations, so that I cannot accidentally staff an opponent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A walk-on staff applicant in competitive play is only ever targeted at a street slot the acting seat owns (`getSlotOwnerId(state, slot) === (state.activePlayerId ?? 0)`), and only when that business has a free employment slot. When the acting seat owns no business with a free slot, no applicant appears (the roll still consumes the day's trigger, exactly as the existing "no eligible business" behaviour).
- `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` and `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` reject a destination business the acting seat does not own, using the shared `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` gate (same `That business belongs to <seat>.` message as upgrades/sell/close); single-player is unchanged because `ownerTaggedGrid` is absent.
- Every employment write path (`hireStaffApplicant`, `placeStaffOnBusiness`, `moveStaffOnBusiness`) defensively refuses to employ a member at a business the acting seat does not own, throwing an error naming the real owner — so a UI/AI/headless caller can never persist the invalid state even if it skips the legality helper.
- Applicant trigger chance and the applicant business-type match pool consider only the acting seat's own businesses (`computeApplicantChance`, `hasEligibleBusiness`, and the type-gate pool in `resolveStaffApplicant`), so an opponent's businesses neither raise the player's applicant chance nor unlock a specialist applicant the player cannot employ.
- A save already carrying player staff employed at another seat's business is repaired on load: the member is released from that business (employment cleared, removed from `employedStaff`, logged in the activity log), remains the player's hired staff, and the repair is idempotent across repeated load/save round-trips.
- New deterministic automated tests cover the owned/unowned matrix — applicant targeting, applicant chance, placement, relocation, the type-match pool, and the save-repair path — built on `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts` (`buildHumanVsAis`) plus existing single-player staff fixtures, and run through the test skill.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (`MainStreetEngineCommands`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner`, `MainStreetStateSerialize` JSDoc), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (hire/relocate rule now states placement is restricted to the acting seat's own businesses), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (shared staff rules sentence), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A competitive player can hire and relocate staff knowing the member works for them — their hire can no longer silently strengthen an AI opponent's business.

## Constraints

- **Single-player must be untouched.** `ownerTaggedGrid` is absent in single-player, so the ownership gate is a no-op there; all existing single-player staff behaviour, tests and Monte Carlo runs must keep passing unchanged.
- **One ownership predicate.** Do not invent a second ownership check: `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` / `getSlotOwnerId` (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`) is the single source of truth and the established idiom for every other cross-owner mutation (upgrade, sell, close, upgrade highlights).
- **Determinism preserved.** Applicant resolution consumes `state.rng`; the fix must not add or reorder RNG draws in ways that change single-player seeded outcomes, and tests must be seeded rather than flaky.
- **No new scope.** Staff salary model, the 1-action relocation cost, the two-type staff model (management-company vs business staff) and the AI's staff-free competitive strategy are unchanged.
- Save-format change (if any) must remain backward compatible: older saves without owner tags load unchanged.

## Existing state

- Shared, owner-tagged street: `state.ownerTaggedGrid` + `getSlotOwnerId` / `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts:26`, `:161`). Every other cross-owner mutation already gates on it (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:313/571/619/769/849`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:174/318`, `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts:159/252`).
- Applicant resolution: `resolveStaffApplicant` → `hasEligibleBusiness` / `pickTargetSlot` / `computeApplicantChance` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1200-1360`) iterate the whole shared grid, with no ownership filter, so `pendingApplicant.targetSlotIndex` can be an AI business. `hireStaffApplicant` (`:1362`) then stamps `employedAtSlot = targetSlotIndex` and pushes onto that business's `employedStaff` with no ownership check.
- Placement/relocation: `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`:962`) checks hired-ness, business-staff type, business-type match and free capacity — but **not** ownership; `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1043`) delegates to it. `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`:1106`) and `moveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1073`) write the employment from those checks only.
- Market-row hires (`purchaseStaffCard`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1059`) never place a member, and `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:922`) has no live UI caller, so the applicant path is the one that can auto-place today; relocation is the other writer.
- Player-facing relocation UI derives destinations from `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `buildMoveStaffAffordance` ~`:603`, used by the Manage-Card dialog and `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:393`), so it currently offers opponent businesses as legal destinations.
- Salaries are charged from the player's `staffCards` (`applyStaffOngoingCosts`), and business-scope buffs resolve from `business.employedStaff` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:322-333`), i.e. the opponent's business is the one that benefits.
- Existing tests: `tests/main-street/staff-placement-commands.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-movement.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/competitive-ownership-actions.test.ts` — none of them covers staff placement against an opponent-owned slot.

## Desired change

1. Filter applicant eligibility, applicant chance and the business-type pool to the acting seat's own business slots (reuse the same ownership predicate, not a local comparison).
2. Add the ownership gate to `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (and therefore `canMoveStaffOnBusiness`), with the owner-naming reason so the UI/tooltip and the activity log read consistently with upgrades and sells.
3. Add a defensive ownership assertion in the employment write paths so no caller can bypass the gate.
4. Repair existing saves that already hold player staff at another seat's business, at load time, with an idempotent and logged release.
5. Cover the matrix (own/opponent × applicant/placement/relocation/chance/type-pool/save-repair) with deterministic tests; update the rules docs and JSDoc.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — ownership filter in `hasEligibleBusiness` / `pickTargetSlot` / `computeApplicantChance` / `resolveStaffApplicant`'s type pool (~`:1200-1330`); `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` gate in `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`:962`); defensive ownership guard in `hireStaffApplicant` (`:1362`) / `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`:1106`) / `moveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1073`); JSDoc.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reference the existing predicate from the new call sites (no new helper expected; extend JSDoc if a staff-specific note is warranted).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — idempotent load-time repair of player staff employed at a slot owned by another seat (plus JSDoc).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — relocation destinations now legitimately exclude opponent businesses (verify no extra change needed beyond the predicate fix).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — applicant hire/decline flow (`:1330-1390`) should surface a clear failure if the pending target is not owned (defensive; target should never be an opponent after the engine fix).
- `tests/main-street/staff-placement-commands.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-movement.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/competitive-ownership-actions.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts` — new owned/unowned matrix coverage.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — state that staff placement/relocation and applicant targeting are restricted to the acting seat's own businesses.

## Related work

- `MS-0MVZC5V6L001OOXN` — *Upgarde highlights should only be the current players businesses* (the precedent fix: ownership gate on a player-facing target picker).
- `MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY` — *Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street* (source of `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`).
- `MS-0MT5X3N79002S038` — *Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play* (staff are player-only in competitive mode, so every member at an AI business is necessarily the player's).
- `MS-0MUOSUNYR0073SI1` — *Gate all staff relocation with 1-action-point cost* and `MS-0MUOSULQ700186PP` — *Update UI and tooltips for free re-roll and staff movement* (relocation paths touched here).
- `MS-0MU3BTSQ8006ZRCU` (staff placement engine/commands, referenced from JSDoc) and CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX (walk-on applicant flow), CG-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1 (per-business `employedStaff` source of truth).
- `MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB` — *two-type staff redesign deltas* (management-company staff are never placed on a business; unchanged here).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUYODDW300690KX** – AI should not place synergies that only benefit the player (completed)
- **MS-0MW2XMA0Z007MZ6D** – Draft two-type staff model in GDD (completed)
- **MS-0MW4MSNMJ006E9JH** – Implement: add skill scope classification and type-consistent assignment (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: business, hired, member, placed, player (+3 more)
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — matched: business, hired, member, placed, player (+2 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: business, hired, placed, player, staff (+1 more)

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — Applicant is filtered, not re-targeted mid-walk.** The applicant simply walks into one of the player's own businesses; we do not add a target picker. Rationale: matches the existing random-target applicant design and needs no new UI.
- **A2 — Applicant chance and the type pool also exclude opponent businesses.** Rationale: the chance formula is `min(income + reputation, 15)`, and counting an opponent's income would both inflate the player's applicant rate and unlock specialists the player cannot employ.
- **A3 — Existing bad saves are repaired on load (release, don't delete).** The member stays hired and unassigned, with an activity-log entry, instead of being left on the opponent's business. Rationale: the saved state is invalid and currently charges the player salary for the opponent's benefit. If the producer prefers "leave the data, let the player relocate it away", AC5 can be dropped without affecting ACs 1–4/6–8.
- **A4 — Scope is ownership only.** No economy rebalance, no change to salary deduction, applicant chance formula shape, or the 1-action relocation cost.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which code path placed the staff in an AI business — market-row hire, walk-on applicant, or relocation?** — Answer (agent, evidence): the walk-on applicant path is the only auto-placing path today (`resolveStaffApplicant` → `hireStaffApplicant`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1282-1390`), because `purchaseStaffCard` never assigns a business and `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` has no live UI caller; relocation is the other unguarded writer (`canMoveStaffOnBusiness`). All three are covered so the report cannot recur through any of them. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Can an AI opponent own/employ staff in competitive mode, i.e. is the reported member unambiguously the player's?** — Answer: yes, staff are player-only in competitive mode (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:2047-2060, 2259-2260, 2345-2346`), so any member on an AI business is a player member. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Should the fix also repair saves already containing the invalid state?** — **OPEN for producer confirmation**; agent assumption A3 applies the load-time release-and-log repair. Source: agent decision, flagged for producer review.
- **Q: Does single-player need any behaviour change?** — Answer: no. `ownerTaggedGrid` is absent in single-player, so `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` is a documented no-op there (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts:161-179`). Source: repo inspection.


## Plan

**Plan: changelog** — generated 2026-11-11 by the plan skill.

Decomposed into five child work items, test-first and vertical-slice ordered:

| Order | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Staff ownership matrix tests (red) (`MS-0MWBCW80F007PJ5M`) | task | — | AC6 |
| 2 | Gate staff placement on slot ownership (`MS-0MWBCWLZY001EA3W`) | feature | 1 | AC2, AC3, AC8 |
| 3 | Ownership-aware staff applicant resolution (`MS-0MWBCWVYC007F6VJ`) | feature | 1 | AC1, AC4, AC8 |
| 4 | Repair cross-seat staff employment on load (`MS-0MWBCX7MS00960BH`) | feature | 1 | AC5, AC8 |
| 5 | Staff ownership docs and full suite (`MS-0MWBCXJK2007KTDB`) | docs | 2, 3, 4 | AC7, AC8 |

- **Vertical slicing:** child 1 is the tracer-bullet red acceptance suite (test-first); children 2–4 each cut through code + tests + JSDoc + activity-log observability for their slice; child 5 is the docs/full-suite verification slice.
- **Effort/risk:** Small / Medium — below the approval gate, so no approval pause was required.
- **Assumption A3** (load-time release-and-log repair) is implemented by child 4; if the producer rejects it, child 4 can be dropped without affecting children 2–3.
- Six automated review stages completed; AC coverage review returned `proceed` (all parent ACs covered by children).

# Full breakdown in tooltips of end of turn dialog

## Problem statement

The end-of-turn ledger tooltips (added by MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO) attach to every
row, but most of them summarise rather than explain: breakdowns are rendered as a
single comma-joined `Per item: A: +5, B: +7` line, the total rows only say "The
sum of the lines above", the supplementary context rows restate their own label,
and no tooltip shows the item's **base value ± each named modifier**. The player
cannot see how a row's total was actually calculated — for example, which part of
a staff member's salary is base and which part is the Operations Manager
discount.

## Users

- **The human player** — reads the Turn Summary after each closing and needs to
  understand exactly how each figure arose, so the next day's decisions are
  informed.
- **Competitive players** — need the same detail on their own seat's tab.

### User stories

- _As a player, I want the Staff wages tooltip to list each staff member on its
  own line with the Base Cost and each +/- modifier (e.g. Operations Manager),
  so I can understand each member's true salary._
- _As a player, I want the income tooltips to list each contributing business on
  its own line, and the Event income tooltip to name each event effect and its
  coins, so I can see what drove my income._
- _As a player, I want the Total rows to list the lines that make them up, so I
  can reconcile the subtotal myself._
- _As a player, I want the Incident and supplementary rows to show the numbers
  behind them, not just a sentence repeating the row label._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff wages** tooltip lists each staff member on its own line, showing the
   base salary and every named modifier with its signed amount (e.g.
   `Operations Manager: -50`), computing the member's charged salary, then
   reconciling the list to the committed category total (including the existing
   street-wide reduction and available-coins clamp lines).
2. **Community spaces** and **Business costs** tooltips list each space/business
   on its own line with its base ongoing cost (not a comma-joined single line),
   still reconciling to the committed category total via the street-wide Cost
   Cutter reduction and clamp lines.
3. **All four income rows** (Base, Synergy, Reputation, Events) list each
   contributing business on its own line; the **Event income** tooltip
   enumerates each event effect (`name: signed delta`) rather than only a
   per-business sum.
4. **Incident** tooltip names the resolved incident and shows each modifier
   applied to its effect (e.g. Brand Ambassador reputation multiplier) so the
   committed coin/reputation deltas are reproducible; the "no incident" note is
   unchanged.
5. **Total income** and **Total operating expenses** tooltips enumerate each
   contributing line with its amount and reconcile to the committed subtotal,
   replacing "The sum of the lines above".
6. **Supplementary context rows** show numeric derivations where the projection
   already carries them: closing coins (day start + net change), reputation
   change (income + incident + one-off reputation) and businesses owned (the
   business names, not just a count). Score change keeps its explanatory text
   because challenge-level detail is not carried by the projection.
7. All new copy is localisable through the existing `t()` / `registerLocale`
   system with English defaults registered at module load; tooltips remain
   **presentational** (no state mutation, no RNG), **absent-safe** (a
   legacy/hand-built ledger with no breakdown degrades to the committed total
   plus the existing explanatory note), and render the same detail level for
   single-player and each competitive seat's tab.
8. Deterministic automated tests cover the enhanced content for every row type
   above (staff modifiers, per-business income lines, event-effect enumeration,
   incident modifiers, total-line enumeration, context derivations), added to
   the existing tooltip suites and run through the test skill.
9. Documentation is updated: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (the
   "End-of-Turn Turn Summary Ledger and Tooltips" per-item detail table and
   tooltip-format description) and the JSDoc in
   `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` / `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Hovering any line in the end-of-turn statement now explains the number behind it
— every staff member's base salary and discounts, every business's contribution,
every event effect, and how the totals add up.

## Constraints

- **Tooltips stay presentational.** No new state mutations and no RNG
  consumption; every figure comes from the committed ledger or the engine's own
  per-item data (`IncomeResult`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`, `state.staffCards`,
  `state.streetGrid`).
- **Do not invent attribution.** Where the ledger carries no per-item data the
  tooltip must fall back to the committed total with an explanatory note, never
  a synthesised split.
- **One-off per-source attribution is out of scope.** `TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas`
  is a residual aggregate; a true per-source breakdown needs engine-level
  attribution in `buildTurnLedger` and is recorded as a follow-up work item.
  The one-off tooltip keeps its documented reconciliation formula.
- **Existing interaction and styling unchanged.** `attachHudTooltipZone` hover/
  tap behaviour, lazy content building, and the `TooltipManager` styling are not
  touched; only content builders and the data threaded into them change.
- **No layout regression.** Multi-line tooltips must fit the existing tooltip
  width/wrapping behaviour; no dialog re-layout.
- **Single-player and competitive parity.** Income detail exists for both;
  competitive expense rows are category-total only today (`OwnerRoundLedger`
  carries no per-card detail) and stay that way unless per-seat detail is
  derived — see A2.

## Existing state

- **Tooltip builders**: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` (334
  lines) — `buildIncomeLineTooltip`, `buildExpenseLineTooltip`,
  `buildTotalLineTooltip`, `buildIncidentLineTooltip`,
  `buildOneOffLineTooltip`, `buildNetLineTooltip`, `buildContextLineTooltip`,
  plus the `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English bundle.
- **Projection model**: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` —
  `PLProjection` / `PLStatementLine` / `PLBreakdownItem` (`{ name, coins }`) /
  `PLLineBreakdown` (`{ items, streetReduction? }`), `incomeLineBreakdown`
  (line 1029) and `expenseLineBreakdown` (line 1070).
- **Data already available**:
  - staff: `state.staffCards[]` with `ongoingCost` and skills;
    `computeStaffSalaryCost` / `computeStaffSalaryDiscount` /
    `getSalaryScopeSkills` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:852-877`), skill name
    `Operations Manager` (`src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts:99`);
  - community / business: `slot.ongoingCost`, `state.streetGrid`,
    `state.soldSlots`;
  - income: `SlotIncome` (`baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) and
    `SlotPhaseBreakdown` (`baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `repBonus`,
    `eventDeltas[]`);
  - incident: `TurnResult.incident` (`EventCard`, carries its base effect) plus
    `incidentCoinChange` / `incidentRepChange`;
  - context: `closingBalances` (day start + net) and `businessesOwned`.
- **Current shallow behaviour** (confirmed by inspection):
  - expenses render comma-joined: `t('...perItem', { breakdown: 'A: -5, B: -7' })`;
  - totals render `label: amount` + "The sum of the lines above.";
  - context rows render a title + one generic sentence, no numbers;
  - the Event income row derives a per-business sum, discarding each
    `SlotEventDelta.name` / `delta`.
- **Tests**: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` (612 lines, unit
  coverage of every builder) and
  `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltip-attachment.test.ts` (attachment), plus
  browser suites `turn-summary-tooltip.browser.test.ts` /
  `turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts`.
- **Docs**: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` § "End-of-Turn Turn Summary
  Ledger and Tooltips" documents the current per-item detail and the one-off
  fallback explicitly.

## Desired change

1. Extend `PLBreakdownItem` with an optional base/adder description so a
   breakdown item can carry `base` plus named `modifiers` while `coins` stays
   the committed contribution. Populate it for staff (`base` = card
   `ongoingCost`, modifier = Operations Manager discount) and leave it absent
   for community/business, where only the base applies.
2. Render expense breakdowns multi-line — one item per line, then the
   reconciling reduction/clamp/total lines.
3. Thread `SlotPhaseBreakdown` detail (including `eventDeltas`) through
   `incomeLineBreakdown` and render income breakdowns multi-line, with the Event
   income row listing each event effect.
4. Add incident modifier detail (reputation-multiplier effects applied to the
   resolved incident) to `buildIncidentLineTooltip`, keeping the `null` fallback.
5. Replace `buildTotalLineTooltip`'s generic note with an enumeration of the
   section's contributing lines and their amounts.
6. Add numeric derivations to the context tooltips that the projection already
   supports (closing coins, reputation change, businesses owned names); leave
   score change as prose.
7. Add the new i18n keys to `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `LEDGER_TOOLTIP_STRINGS`
   and update the docs table.
8. Add/extend deterministic tests for each enhanced builder and for the threaded
   model data.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — multi-line breakdown rendering,
  incident modifier detail, total-line enumeration, context derivations, new
  i18n keys. Replaces the comma-joining `formatBreakdown`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend `PLBreakdownItem` (base +
  modifiers), thread `eventDeltas` / `repBonus` through `incomeLineBreakdown`,
  supply staff base/modifier detail in `expenseLineBreakdown`, extend
  `PLSupplementaryContext` for day-start coins and business names.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — pass the section's lines to
  `buildTotalLineTooltip` and the extra context data; no interaction change
  expected beyond the call sites.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — per-row-type content
  assertions (staff base ± modifier, per-business income lines, event effects,
  incident modifiers, total enumeration, context derivations).
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-model.test.ts` — model-level assertions for
  the new breakdown/modifier fields and absent-safe degradation.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — per-item detail table and tooltip
  format description.

## Related work

- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — *Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger* (parent: attached
  the tooltips this item deepens).
- `MS-0MW7QQ5QU007XXC0` — *Attach tooltips to the Turn Summary ledger rows*.
- `MS-0MW7QQ1FD000RCA3` — *Verification: ledger tooltip model and content*.
- `MS-0MW7QQ65P006N3KA` — *Competitive per-seat tooltip parity*.
- `MS-0MW7QQ5BX002KGS0` — *Extend P&L model with per-item breakdowns and tooltip
  content* (the projection/breakdown plumbing this item deepens).
- `MS-0MWBZ05LB007UXQ9` — *Build Summary-row tooltip content builders* (blocked:
  the Summary tab's per-figure tooltips will reuse the per-line builders this
  item improves, so its breakdowns inherit the new detail automatically).
- `MS-0MW6H9A47001B1QT` — *Cards should represent the actual income and
  reputation changes* (same principle of showing the engine's real per-item
  figures rather than card-face values).
- `MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ` — *two-type staff skills* (Operations Manager salary
  discount and its business-staff gating).
- `MS-0MW2XMA0Z007MZ6D` — *Draft two-type staff model in GDD*.

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — "Break down the line" means one contributing item per line, with base
  ± named modifiers where the data exists.** For staff that is the base salary
  and the Operations Manager discount; for community/business it is the base
  ongoing cost (the only per-item modifier is street-wide, already a separate
  line). **Recommended** choice, matching the producer's Staff wages example.
- **A2 — Competitive expense rows remain category-total only.** Income detail is
  already per-seat; deriving per-card expense detail for each competitive seat
  would need owner-filtered street/staff derivation and is deferred (recorded as
  a follow-up). Detail level for income/incident/totals/context is identical on
  every tab.
- **A3 — One-off keeps the reconciliation formula.** A per-source split requires
  engine attribution in `buildTurnLedger`; recorded as a follow-up work item
  rather than expanded into this one.
- **A4 — Score change keeps prose.** The projection carries the net score delta
  but not the challenge-level detail needed to show its constituents; extending
  the ledger for that is out of scope.
- **A5 — No layout change.** Multi-line content is assumed to fit the existing
  tooltip width/wrap; if it does not, wrapping is the implementer's call (no
  dialog re-layout).

**Risks**

- *Divergence risk*: re-deriving per-item figures in the UI instead of reading
  the committed ledger could drift from the engine. Mitigation: derive only from
  the engine's own helpers (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `SlotPhaseBreakdown`) and
  keep the reconcile-to-committed-total lines so any drift is visible in the
  tooltip itself.
- *Regression risk to prior tooltip work*: the parent suite asserts current copy.
  Mitigation: update the assertions deliberately alongside the copy change, and
  keep every existing behaviour (hover/tap, lazy build, absent-safe fallback).
- *Scope-creep risk*: the producer's "each one" could pull in one-off attribution
  and competitive per-card expenses. Mitigation: explicit A2/A3 decisions above,
  with the deferred work linked as follow-up items rather than absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which rows are in scope — every tooltip, or only expenses?** — Answer
  (agent, from seed context + inspection): the seed requests a full breakdown of
  each line ("Staff wages should list each staff member, one per line, with the
  Base Cost +/- any adjustments"). Scope covers income lines, expense lines,
  incident, totals, and the derivable context rows; one-off and score change are
  excluded (A3/A4). Source: seed description; repo inspection of
  `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`.
- **Q: Should a breakdown be one item per line, or is the existing
  comma-separated list acceptable?** — Answer (agent): one item per line, with
  base ± named modifiers, matching the producer's example. **Recommended:**
  one item per line — the comma-joined format is what the producer described as
  "simply repeat the line". Source: seed description.
- **Q: How should the one-off row be broken down?** — **OPEN QUESTION for the
  producer.** `TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas` stores only a residual
  (`netCoinChange - incomeCoins - ongoingTotal - incidentCoinChange`); there is no
  per-source data (market purchases/sales, event plays, Community Favour) to
  attribute. **Recommended:** keep the reconciliation formula here and create a
  follow-up item for engine-level attribution — this keeps the current item
  shippable and avoids inventing splits. Source: `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
  (`oneOffDeltas`) and the existing documented fallback in
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.
- **Q: Does competitive mode need per-card expense breakdowns?** — Answer
  (agent): income detail is already per-seat; `OwnerRoundLedger` carries no
  per-card expense detail, so deriving it would be new work. **Recommended:**
  defer to a follow-up (A2) and keep income/incident/totals/context at parity on
  every tab. Source: `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` (`buildExpenseRows`).
- **Q: Are single-player and competitive both affected?** — Answer: yes; the same
  builders render every tab, so both benefit wherever the data exists. Source:
  `MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` statement body.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MW3O2O0V00042E5** – Out-of-actions dialog overlay with End Turn/Dismiss and enable checkbox (completed)
- **MS-0MWBZ05LB007UXQ9** – Build Summary-row tooltip content builders (blocked)
- **MS-0MW6H9A47001B1QT** – Cards should represent the actual income and reputation changes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: apply, base, break, breakdown, calculated (+26 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: adjustments, apply, base, break, breakdown (+26 more)

data.description:
**Headline:** Give management-company staff a visible home — a hoverable Staff Pile to the left of the hand that shows the hires as stacked card faces plus a portrait row and summarises the management team in a tooltip.

## Problem statement

The game ships a two-type staff model — **business staff** (carry an `employedAtSlot` link and buff one business) and **management-company staff** (no slot; player/turn-scoped hand-slot, action-point, market and incident effects) — yet management-company staff have **no persistent surface in the UI**. Once hired they vanish from the board: the player can only infer them from hand capacity, action counts and tooltips on unrelated HUD elements. The player cannot see *who* works for their management company or summarise the management team at a glance. This work item adds a **Staff Pile** to the UI, to the left of the hand against the left edge, which holds the management-company staff and summarises them on hover.

## Users

- **Main Street player (hands-on)** — hires management-company staff and needs to see the company's management team and what each member does without opening a dialog.
  - As a player, I want to see my hired management-company staff as soon as I hire them, so that the hire has a visible result.
  - As a player, I want to hover the pile and read a summary of every management-company staff member (role, benefit, salary, total), so that I can plan the next hire against the current team.
- **Main Street player (new / learning)** — is taught that staff come in two forms; the pile makes the management-company half of the roster concrete.
  - As a new player, I want the management-company staff I own collected in one labelled place, so that I understand which staff belong to my company rather than to a business.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs a visible, inspectable roster surface to verify management-company hires, salary totals and hand-slot/action effects.
  - As QA, I want the pile's count and tooltip totals to match `state.staffCards`, so that I can verify staffing state visually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Staff Pile renders to the left of the hand, against the left edge, positioned from a new `staffPile` zone in the SLL layout authority (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`) with a matching zone in the tutorial layout — no hard-coded pixel offsets.
- The pile displays **only management-company staff** (staff in `state.staffCards` for which `isBusinessStaffCard(card)` is false) as a fanned/stacked set of small card faces (newest hire on top) with a count badge, and a small portrait row beneath the stack.
- Hovering the pile — the stack or the portrait row beneath it — shows a tooltip that lists every management-company staff member in the company with name, role/benefit summary and salary, plus the total count; the tooltip covers management-company staff only (business staff are excluded).
- The pile updates on every refresh that changes staffing (hire, lay-off, `maxHandSize` change), is hidden when the company has no management-company staff, and never overlaps the hand capacity row or the hand panel at any supported `maxHandSize`.
- The pile has no lay-off control of its own; its only click affordance is opening the company roster overlay (`MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA`) from the stack or the portrait row, and every lay-off action lives in that roster. *(Amended during intake of MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA at the producer's direction: the roster's entry point is the pile; the pile work itself still renders, positions and hovers exactly as specified above.)*
- Automated tests cover the management-company selection and the tooltip content (unit) and the pile's placement, count badge, hover tooltip and empty-state hiding (browser/render), including a capacity case at the largest supported hand size.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players can see at a glance who works for their management company — and hover for a full summary of the management team — instead of inferring their staff from hand size and action counts.

## Constraints

- **Display-only.** No new gameplay rules, engine commands or state fields: the pile is derived from `state.staffCards` on each render. Lay-off from the pile is out of scope.
- **Two-type model stays authoritative.** Membership is decided by the existing helper (`!isBusinessStaffCard(card)`), never by a new persisted flag or a card-name list.
- **Hover-only interactivity.** The pile must not intercept pointer input beyond the tooltip: hand-card clicks, hand→street drags and market→hand drops under/around the pile behave exactly as today.
- **Layout is SLL-first.** Geometry comes from a new layout zone resolved by `MainStreetLayoutAdapter`; the tutorial layout keeps parity so tutorial screenshots/highlights do not drift.
- **No overlap budget.** The pile is constrained to the free band left of the capacity row, including the widest hand the game can reach, at the 1280×720 base viewport.
- **Reuse existing rendering and formatting.** Card faces/portraits reuse the shared SVG card renderer (`mainStreetRenderCardSvg`); per-member summary lines reuse or mirror `formatEmployedStaffSummary`.
- **Localisation.** New tooltip strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern; no hard-coded user-visible strings.
- **Accessibility parity.** The pile's hover target follows the existing HUD tooltip accessibility pattern; no new input modality is introduced.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `state.staffCards` holds every hired staff member. Business staff carry `employedAtSlot`; management-company staff do not. `isBusinessStaffCard()` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`) is the canonical type test; `getStreetScopeSkills()` already filters on it.
- Hired staff currently have **no** persistent UI surface: management-company staff are visible only through derived effects and tooltip text. Business staff appear via a corner count badge on their business slot (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`).
- The hand is a bottom-anchored capacity row: `handCenterX` is centred on the street block, and `drawHandPanel()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`) draws one persistent, non-interactive panel sized `maxSlots × (handCardW + HAND_SLOT_PITCH_PAD)`, rebuilt from `refreshPlayerHand()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts`.
- Zone positions come from the SLL authority (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`, parsed in `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`); the tutorial layout is `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` enforces its required zones.
- Hover tooltips use `s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()` with pure content builders in `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`; staff summary lines already exist in `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`).
- There is **no** company-roster UI: `letGoStaffCommand` is wired only to the business Manage-Card dialog, which enumerates `employedAtSlot === slotIndex`, so management-company staff cannot currently be let go from the UI.

## Desired change

Add a **Staff Pile** in the free band left of the hand:

- A new `staffPile` SLL zone (plus tutorial parity) resolved into `SceneLayout` (`staffPileX`, `staffPileY`, and presentation sizes).
- A new renderer step (`drawStaffPile()`) on the hand-refresh path that rebuilds the pile from `state.staffCards`' management-company members: a fanned/stacked set of small card faces (newest on top) with a count badge, and a small portrait row beneath the stack. Hidden when the set is empty.
- A pure tooltip builder (`buildStaffPileTooltip(state)`) returning a management-company-only summary: one line per member (name, role/benefit, salary) and the total count, wired to hover on the pile.
- Tests and documentation as per the acceptance criteria.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — Needs a new `staffPile` zone (top-left anchored in the band left of `hand`).
- `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` — Needs the matching `staffPile` zone for tutorial parity.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — Needs to resolve the `staffPile` zone into `SceneLayout` fields.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — Needs new `SceneLayout` pile fields plus presentation constants (stack offsets, portrait size, panel padding).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — Needs `drawStaffPile()` declared alongside `drawHandPanel()`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Needs to delegate `drawStaffPile()` to the implementation module.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — New module implementing the pile render, count badge and hover wiring (mirroring the `drawHandPanel` lifecycle).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — Needs to call `renderer.drawStaffPile()` on the hand-refresh path so hires/lay-offs/`maxHandSize` changes are reflected.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — Needs a pure `buildStaffPileTooltip(state)` builder plus new i18n keys/strings.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Needs a management-company staff summary formatter (reuse or extract from `formatEmployedStaffSummary`).
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — Provides `isBusinessStaffCard()` for membership (reference; no behaviour change expected).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — Provides `mainStreetRenderCardSvg` for the small card faces/portraits (reference; possibly a portrait helper).
- `tests/main-street/staff-pile.test.ts` — New unit tests for membership selection and tooltip content.
- `tests/main-street/staff-pile.browser.test.ts` — New render tests for placement, count, hover tooltip, empty-state hiding and max-capacity non-overlap.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` / `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` — Anchor/zone contracts to extend for `staffPile`.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Needs the Staff Pile UI specification (position, contents, hover behaviour, overlap budget).
- `src/README.md` — Needs the new renderer module and layout zone noted.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Staff impact (completed): the two-type staff redesign that defines management-company staff.
- **MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT** — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (completed): scope gate now applied by `isBusinessStaffCard`.
- **MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ** — Scope gate in buff aggregation (completed): the helpers that already filter management-company members.
- **MS-0MWBB146L005SU31** — Player hired staff, staff went to AI business (in progress): competitive-mode staff ownership bug, separate from this display work.
- **MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY** — Turn summary P&L statement (completed): staff expense lines, a nearby presentation precedent.
- **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** — Company roster overlay: view and lay off management-company staff (open, discovered-from this item): the deferred click/roster/lay-off half.
- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4, D.4.2 §5 company roster lay-off), `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (action/hand mechanics).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — overlap with the hand:** the pile shares the bottom band with a hand that grows with `maxHandSize`. *Mitigation:* place it from a dedicated SLL zone in the free left band and add a max-capacity non-overlap test.
- **Risk — input interception:** an interactive pile could swallow hand-card clicks/drags. *Mitigation:* keep the pile non-interactive except a hover hit area confined to the pile's own bounds; assert hand click/drag paths in the browser test.
- **Risk — scope creep into a roster/lay-off UI:** *Mitigation:* explicit constraint that the pile is display-only; the roster is MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.
- **Risk — duplicated staff-summary formatting** between the business-slot tooltip and the pile tooltip. *Mitigation:* reuse or extract `formatEmployedStaffSummary` rather than writing a second formatter.
- **Assumption:** the pile is hidden entirely when the company employs no management-company staff (no placeholder tile).
- **Assumption:** "management-company staff" is exactly `state.staffCards` filtered by `!isBusinessStaffCard(card)`; business staff never appear on the pile.
- **Assumption:** "a small portrait row below" is an additional row of small member portraits beneath the card-face stack; hovering either the stack or the row shows the tooltip (interpretation recorded in the Appendix).
- **Assumption:** the pile needs no new art assets — card faces and portraits reuse the existing SVG renderer.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Visual form of the pile — A. fanned/stacked small card faces with a count badge; B. a single decorative pile tile with count badge only; C. a compact portrait row with count badge." **Recommended:** A.
  - Answer (producer): "A with a small portrait row below which, when hovered over triggers the tooltip". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: option A — fanned/stacked small card faces with a count badge — **plus** a small portrait row beneath the stack; hovering the pile shows the tooltip.
  - Research: the roster is small (9 management-company roles in GDD D.4.4), and `mainStreetRenderCardSvg` already renders card faces at arbitrary sizes, so a stack plus portrait row is achievable without new art.
- Q2: "Tooltip scope — A. all staff (management-company plus business staff grouped by business); B. management-company staff only." **Recommended:** A.
  - Answer (producer): "Management Company only". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: B. The tooltip lists management-company staff only. (This supersedes the seed description's "all staff in the company".)
- Q3: "Interactivity — A. hover tooltip only, roster/lay-off as a separate follow-up; B. hover tooltip plus click-to-open a company roster enabling lay-off." **Recommended:** A.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A. Hover tooltip only; the company roster and lay-off path is deferred to MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.
- Q (no producer input needed — resolved by repo research): "Does a company-roster/lay-off UI already exist for management-company staff?" — Answer (agent, research): no; `letGoStaffCommand` is wired only to the business Manage-Card dialog (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`), which enumerates `employedAtSlot === slotIndex`. Evidence: grep of `letGoStaffCommand` call sites. Recorded because it motivated the deferred follow-up.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** – Company roster overlay: view and lay off management-company staff (open)
- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** – Staff impact (completed)
- **MS-0MW2XMA0Z007MZ6D** – Draft two-type staff model in GDD (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, accessibility, action, add, additional (+393 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mw4xula90002oey, acceptance, accessibility, action, add (+365 more)
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: action, add, additional, adds, alongside (+302 more)

## Plan (decomposition)

**Phasing — three vertical slices, each end-to-end (layout → render → verify):**

1. **Slice 1 — position** (`MS-0MWC7NU7W006ZI3X`): `staffPile` SLL zone in both layouts, `SceneLayout` pile fields, adapter resolution, plus the anchor/tutorial-layout tests. Deliverable: the pile's geometry resolves from layout authority data with no hard-coded offsets.
2. **Slice 2 — content** (`MS-0MWC7ZDP3002ULBD`, `MS-0MWC7Z6OF008J0PP`): the pure tooltip builder (independent, runnable in parallel) and the renderer module that draws the stack, count badge, portrait row and hover wiring on the hand-refresh path. Deliverable: a visible, hoverable pile that summarises the management team.
3. **Slice 3 — verification & handoff** (`MS-0MWC7ZISD003MOU7`, `MS-0MWC7ZOCK009RRUQ`, `MS-0MWC7ZTEH003ZKYY`): unit tests for selection and tooltip content, browser/render tests for placement, count, hover, empty state, refresh and max-capacity non-overlap, then documentation.

**Dependency order**

```
MS-0MWC7NU7W006ZI3X  Layout plumbing: staffPile zones + SceneLayout   -- start here
   └─ MS-0MWC7Z6OF008J0PP  Staff Pile renderer module
MS-0MWC7ZDP3002ULBD  Tooltip builder (MC-only summary, i18n)          -- independent, parallel
   ├─ MS-0MWC7ZISD003MOU7  Unit tests (selection + tooltip content)   -- needs 3, 2
   ├─ MS-0MWC7ZOCK009RRUQ  Browser/render tests                       -- needs 1, 2, 3
      └─ MS-0MWC7ZTEH003ZKYY  Documentation                           -- needs 2, 3, 4, 5
```

**Between slices:** re-read the next slice's child description and correct it against what the previous slice actually shipped (the resolved `staffPile` pixel box, the final tooltip line format, the rendered depths) before starting it.

**Effort/risk:** Medium effort / Medium risk — ~26.5 h recommended (PERT O=13.5, M=19.5, P=31.5 h), risk score 7/25. Per-child effort: layout 3.2 h, renderer 6.3 h, tooltip 3.2 h, unit tests 2.1 h, browser tests 4.2 h, docs 1.6 h.

## Appendix: plan session (questions, answers, open questions)

- No new producer questions were needed: the intake answers (Q1 stack + portrait row, Q2 management-company-only tooltip, Q3 hover-only) already determine the decomposition.
- **OPEN QUESTION (producer) — overlap budget at wide hands.** `maxHandSize` has no hard cap (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`: "starts at 3, growable via management-company staff handSlotsAdded (no hard cap)"). Hiring every management-company staff card adds 14 slots (Assistant 2, Manager 1, Director 3, Apprentice 1, Socialite 1, Accountant 1, General Manager 4, Lookout 1; Executive 0), so `maxHandSize` can reach 17 — a capacity row of 17 × (140 + 8) ≈ 2516 px centred on `handCenterX`, wider than the 1280×720 viewport. The intake AC "never overlaps the hand capacity row or the hand panel at any supported `maxHandSize`" therefore cannot hold literally for the widest hands.
  - Evidence: `src/MainStreetConstants.ts` (`BASE_HAND_CARD_W = 140`, `HAND_SLOT_PITCH_PAD = 8`); `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts::drawHandPanel()` (width `maxSlots × (handCardW + 8)`, centred on `handCenterX`); `core/src/ui/HandView.ts` (fixed pitch — the row never shrinks or wraps).
  - Interim interpretation applied in `MS-0MWC7ZOCK009RRUQ`: assert non-overlap at the largest hand size whose capacity row still leaves a free band at 1280×720 (documented as `maxHandSize ≤ 8`); beyond that the pile stays inside its `staffPile` zone and the hand panel stays behind it in z-order.
  - Why it matters: it decides whether a wide-hand fallback is needed (clamp the pile, lift it above the hand band, or accept overlap). It does not block the layout, renderer or tooltip work.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-11 — re-plan after an interrupted planning run: reused the six existing children (no duplicates), rewrote `MS-0MWC7NU7W006ZI3X` (its `Key Files` and inline paths had been stripped by a backtick-escaping fault), restated each child's acceptance criteria against the parent ACs (AC coverage 0% → 100%), moved all six children to stage `intake_complete`, removed one duplicated plan comment, and recorded the wide-hand overlap OPEN QUESTION above.
- 2026-11-11 — initial decomposition into six children in test-aware dependency order (superseded description was unchanged; this run only repaired and verified it).
