data.description:
Add a true **Summary** tab to the end-of-turn Turn Summary overlay: the first tab, selected by default, showing only the closed turn's headline information — what each player/AI did, what happened (events), and how income/reputation/score moved — with each figure carrying a tooltip that breaks it down the way today's per-player tab does.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary overlay opens on one player's full profit/loss statement, so the first thing a player sees is a dense per-account breakdown rather than what actually happened in the turn. There is no single view that answers "who did what, what happened, and did everyone gain or lose?" — the player must tab through every seat and read four sections per seat to assemble that picture.

## Users

- **Single-player player** — wants a one-glance recap of the day ("I placed a business, an incident hit, I earned +18 and my score is 42") without reading a full P&L.
- **Competitive player** — wants to see, in one place, what each rival did this shared day and how each seat's income, reputation and score moved, before drilling into any one seat's statement.
- **AI seats (as presented subjects)** — their actions, events and deltas must appear in the same summary so a competitive turn reads as a shared day, not just the human's day.

Example user stories:

- As a single-player player, I open the Turn Summary and immediately see my major actions, the incident that hit, and my income/reputation/score change with my resulting balances.
- As a competitive player, I open the Turn Summary and see every seat's major actions for the shared day plus each seat's income/reputation/score change and balance, then hover any figure to see that seat's breakdown.
- As a player who wants detail, I switch from `[ Summary ]` to `[ You ]` / `[ AI 1 ]` and get exactly today's full profit/loss statement for that seat.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Turn Summary overlay presents a `[ Summary ]` tab as its **first** tab and selects it by default, in both single-player and competitive closings, leaving the existing per-player tabs (`You` / `AI n`) unchanged and still selectable.
- The Summary tab's sections render in the confirmed order **Major actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score** (producer answer Q1 = A).
- The Summary tab lists the closed turn's **major actions** — player- and AI-initiated actions only (placing a business, hiring staff, playing an upgrade/event, moving a card to hand, selling, laying off, closing a street card, loans, challenge completions) — per seat, attributed with the seat label (`You` / `AI n`) used elsewhere in the UI. Turn headers and the turn's own monetary summary rows (income/reputation lines) are excluded, because the sections below already present those figures (producer answer Q2). The list is derived from the game's own record of what happened that turn, not from UI-invented figures.
- Action classification is structural, not textual: the turn record exposes an explicit action marker (an optional category on `LogEntry`, set wherever a player- or AI-initiated action is logged), so no rendered action row depends on matching log message text.
- The Summary tab shows the day's **income change and resulting balance**, **reputation change and resulting balance** and **score change and resulting balance**, one row per metric with every player/AI seat's change and closing balance listed on that row (producer answer Q3 = A), formatted with the panel's existing signed convention (`+N` / `-N` / `0`).
- The Summary tab shows the turn's **events** (the resolved incident and the effect it applied) as their own labelled section, rendered **before** the income/reputation/score figures (producer answer Q1 = A).
- Every seat's figure on the Summary tab carries a hover/tap tooltip giving that seat's **breakdown** equivalent to today's per-player tab (per-business income phases, per-card expense categories, incident/one-off reconciliation, net reconciliation), and the tooltip figures reconcile to the headline figure they annotate.
- The Summary tab participates in tab navigation: pointer selection, Left/Right keyboard cycling and the selected-tab preservation after a mid-game loan take all include it, and selection is signalled with the panel's existing bold-selected convention.
- Every seat's tab label is legible on the panel's black background: a seat colour that falls below WCAG AA contrast against it (the colour-blind-safe palette's Okabe–Ito black, `#000000`) is lightened toward white by `ensureReadableSeatColour()` while a colour that already clears the ratio is drawn unchanged, so a `[ You ]` or `[ AI n ]` tab can never become invisible (audit-rejection fix: the producer saw the AI tabs but no `You` tab).
- Presentation-only and absent-safe: no state mutation, no RNG consumption, no new persisted field; a result carrying no ledger of either shape still advances the closing immediately instead of stranding it; reduced-motion, replay and headless pacing are unchanged.
- Unit tests cover a pure Summary-tab model builder: the confirmed section order, per-seat action attribution (player and AI), exclusion of turn headers and monetary summary rows from the actions section, one-row-per-metric layout with a change and a balance per seat, signed formatting, absent-safe degradation when the turn record omits actions/events, and reconciliation of headline figures with the existing P&L projection.
- Browser (Phaser/jsdom) tests cover the Summary tab being first and default-selected in both modes, its rendered sections, its tooltips on hover/tap, tab switching away and back, and the selected Summary tab surviving a post-loan-take re-render.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably the Turn Summary sections of `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players now open the Turn Summary on a single headline view of the day — who did what, what happened, and how everyone's income, reputation and score moved — instead of a dense per-player account, while the full breakdown stays one hover (or one tab) away.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only: the summary is projected from already-committed turn data; no accounting is recomputed by the UI and no new authoritative figure is introduced.
- Reuse, don't fork: the existing P&L projection (`PLProjection`) and the existing tooltip content builders (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`) stay the single source of breakdown truth so the Summary and per-player tabs can never drift.
- Overlay pattern compliance (`AGENTS.md` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201, dismissal via `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX through `safePlaySound`.
- Panel geometry is fixed (`PANEL_WIDTH` 680 × `PANEL_HEIGHT` 640): the summary layout must stay within it for a full competitive roster (the section must reflow or bound its row count rather than overflow).
- All new user-facing strings go through the core-engine `t()` i18n path, matching the existing ledger tooltip keys; UK English spelling.
- Action classification is structural, not textual: add an optional action marker to `LogEntry` and set it at every player- or AI-initiated action `addLog` call site; no rendered action row may depend on matching log message text.

## Existing state

- The overlay is one unified tabbed P&L panel: `presentTurnSummaryPanel()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`, entered from `showTurnSummaryDialog()` (single-player) and `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog()` (competitive). Tabs are built by `buildPLTabsFromTurnSummary()` / `buildPLTabsFromCompetitiveSummary()`, each tab body rendered from a `PLProjection`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` is the Phaser-free model: `buildTurnSummary()` (single-player headline figures), `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary()` (per-seat rows), `buildPLProjection()` / `buildPLFromTurnSummary()` / `buildPLFromCompetitiveRow()` (the statement), `buildPLTabs*()` (the tab strip).
- Per-row breakdowns already exist: `PLLineBreakdown` carries per-business income items and per-card expense items, and `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` builds the tooltip content (`buildIncomeLineTooltip`, `buildExpenseLineTooltip`, `buildIncidentLineTooltip`, `buildOneOffLineTooltip`, `buildNetLineTooltip`, `buildTotalLineTooltip`, `buildContextLineTooltip`).
- The turn's narrative record already exists: `state.activityLog` (`LogEntry[]`, each with `turn`, `text`, `type`, and optional `seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`), written solely through `appendActivityLogEntry()` in `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts`, with `addLog()` (seat-attributed) and `addLogShared()` (turn-level) as the two producers. It carries player-initiated actions (place business, hire staff, play upgrade/event, move to hand, sell, lay off, close, loans, challenge completions) **mixed with** monetary summary rows (per-turn income/reputation lines) and turn headers.
- The resolved incident is on the result (`TurnResult.incident`, an `EventCard | null`, plus `incidentCoinChange` / `incidentRepChange`); the competitive ledger does not name the incident, so competitive summary rows carry `incidentName: null` today.
- Existing tests to extend: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-model.test.ts`, `turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`, `turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts`, `turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts`, `turn-summary-tooltip.browser.test.ts`, `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Model** — a pure builder (in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) producing a Summary-tab model in the confirmed order: per-seat major actions (player- and AI-initiated only), the turn's events, then one row per metric (Income / Reputation / Score) carrying every seat's change and closing balance, each figure paired with the `PLProjection`-derived tooltip payload it annotates. Absent-safe: a turn record missing actions or events yields empty sections, never a thrown error.
2. **Overlay** — a `[ Summary ]` tab inserted before the per-player tabs and marked default; its body renders the model's sections with per-figure tooltip zones (`attachHudTooltipZone`), inside the existing panel geometry.
3. **Tooltips** — extend `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` with the content builders the Summary tab needs, reusing the existing per-line builders so a summary tooltip's breakdown matches that seat's per-player tab.
4. **Action classification** — source the major-action rows from `state.activityLog` for the closed turn, selected by a new optional action marker on `LogEntry` that every player- and AI-initiated action `addLog` call site sets; turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows carry no marker, so they never appear in the actions section (producer answer Q2).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — new pure Summary-tab model builder alongside `buildTurnSummary()` / `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary()`; reuse `PLProjection` for tooltip payloads.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — insert the `[ Summary ]` tab, mark it default, render its body and attach its tooltips within the fixed panel geometry.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — Summary-row tooltip content builders and their i18n keys (reusing the existing per-line builders).
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — optional structural action marker on `LogEntry` (producer answer Q2).
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` and the `addLog` call sites for player-/AI-initiated actions — set the marker (turn headers and monetary summary rows deliberately leave it unset).
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-summary-tab*.test.ts` — new unit/browser suites; extend `turn-summary-pl-overlay.browser.test.ts` for tab-strip parity.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Turn Summary dialog and competitive panel sections document the new default tab.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY** — Turn summary should be laid out as an account profit/loss statement (completed): parent of the tabbed P&L overlay this tab extends; its producer answers (Q1=A, Q2=A, Q3=A) fix the statement shape and the human-default tab this item now supersedes as the default view.
- **MS-0MW5ER6HC000HVQ8** — Implement tabbed P&L overlay (completed): the tab strip, rendering and keyboard navigation being extended here.
- **MS-0MW5EQ0BA004E4QY** / **MS-0MW5EPEXW000AZKO** — P&L projection model and its unit tests: the breakdown source the Summary tab's tooltips reuse.
- **MS-0MW7QQ5QU007XXC0** / **MS-0MW7QQ65P006N3KA** / **MS-0MW7QQ286007L4J3** — ledger row tooltips, competitive per-seat tooltip parity and their browser verification: the tooltip attachment contract the Summary tab must follow.
- **MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO** / **MS-0MW6GPRL6001DFCF** — end-of-turn ledger tooltips and the pointer-blocker fix: existing panel interaction behaviour that must not regress.
- **MS-0MW5ERPLV004WZHR** — Update Turn Summary documentation (completed): the docs section to extend.
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** — Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (completed): the single-presentation-path constraint.
- **MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK** / **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** — competitive per-seat summary rows and the competitive end-of-turn summary dialog epic: competitive parity for the new tab.
- Related docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate; Competitive Turn Summary panel), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/dev/testing.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Section order (confirmed).** Producer answer Q1 = A: Major actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score. The seed's numbering is superseded by its own "events (before income/reputation/score)" note; browser assertions pin this order.
- **"Major action" scope (confirmed).** Producer answer Q2: player- and AI-initiated actions only — turn headers and the per-turn monetary summary rows are excluded so the section never repeats the figures shown below it.
- **Classification integrity (medium).** The activity log mixes action rows with monetary summary rows, so the new `LogEntry` action marker is the only discriminator. Mitigation: a guard test that every action-producing call site sets the marker, plus an absent-safe model path that renders an empty actions section rather than guessing.
- **Panel overflow (medium).** A summary tab with a full competitive roster (actions + events + 3×N figures) can exceed the fixed 680×640 panel. Mitigation: bounded row counts with an "…and N more" affordance, compact typography, and a browser test at maximum supported roster size.
- **Drift between Summary and per-player tabs (medium).** Two renderings of the same figures can diverge. Mitigation: both project from the same `PLProjection` / model values; unit tests assert reconciliation.
- **Existing tooltip/pointer behaviour regressions (low-medium).** Tooltip attachment, tap-toggle and the `[ Next Turn ]` pointer blocker are pinned by earlier items. Mitigation: extend the existing browser suites rather than writing parallel ones.
- **Scope creep.** Live activity-log feed behaviour, incident-balance rules, the loan selector and the competitive closing animation are out of scope; any new opportunity found during implementation becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption.** The Summary tab appears in both single-player and competitive closings (the panel is one shared renderer); single-player shows a single `You` row set with a non-interactive tab strip as today.
- **Assumption.** "Events" means the resolved incident and the effect it applied (the panel already carries `TurnResult.incident` plus its coin/reputation deltas); played event cards surface through the actions section as player-initiated actions rather than a second events list. If the producer wants drawn/played event cards in the Events section too, that is an additive change to the same section.
- **Assumption.** The Income/Reputation/Score rows show the human seat plus every non-eliminated AI seat in competitive play, and the single `You` seat in single-player — the same seat set the tab strip already shows.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Section order — does "events (before income/reputation/score)" mean the Events section renders **above** the income/reputation/score figures, or that events merely resolve before them in the turn sequence (keeping the seed's numbered order: actions → figures → events)? — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — Actions → Events → Income/Reputation/Score.** Recorded in the ACs and pinned by the browser assertions. Source: producer reply on this work item.
- Q: "Major actions" scope — which activity-log rows belong in the Summary tab? (a) player-initiated actions only, excluding the per-turn income/reputation summary rows the tab already presents; (b) every activity-log row for the turn; (c) every row including turn headers. — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **player- and AI-initiated actions** — i.e. option (a), actions only, covering every seat. Turn headers and monetary summary rows stay out. Implemented structurally via the new `LogEntry` action marker. Source: producer reply on this work item.
- Q: Income/reputation/score layout on the Summary tab — (a) one row per metric listing each seat's change and balance (each seat segment its own tooltip); (b) one block per player with three metric rows; (c) a full grid of player × metric rows. — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — one row per metric**, with every seat's change and resulting balance on that row and a per-seat tooltip. Source: producer reply on this work item.
- Q: Should the Summary tab be the default view in competitive closings as well as single-player? — Answer (agent, researched): **Yes** — single-player and competitive closings share one renderer (`presentTurnSummaryPanel`), and the seed asks for a summary of "players/AI", so the tab is first and default in both modes. Research: `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` → *Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate*.

- Turn headers and per-turn monetary summary rows (income/reputation lines) carry no `action` marker.

- Add optional `action?: string` to the `LogEntry` interface.

- Leave turn headers and monetary summary rows unset.

None — this is a foundational, additive change.

# Attribute one-off ledger deltas to their source for the Turn Summary tooltip

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary one-off row presents only a reconciliation formula
(`net change − income − expenses − incident`) because
`TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas` / `OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffDeltas` store a **residual**
with no per-source attribution. The player cannot see whether the one-off came
from market purchases, market sales, event plays, Community Favour exchanges,
or loan effects.

## Users

- **The human player** — wants to understand what caused a positive or negative
  one-off figure in the Turn Summary, so they can plan MarketPhase actions more
  effectively on the next day.
- **Competitive players** — want the same attribution on their own seat's one-off
  row in the competitive panel.

### User stories

- _As a player, I want the Turn Summary one-off tooltip to list each source
  (market purchase, market sale, event play, Community Favour, loan effect)
  with its signed amount, so I can see what drove the one-off figure._
- _As a competitive player, I want my own seat's one-off row to show the same
  per-source attribution as the single-player panel._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **TurnLedger gains a `oneOffBreakdown` field** — an array of `{ label: string; coins: number; reputation: number }` entries, alongside the existing residual `oneOffDeltas` (which stays for reconciliation and absent-safe fallback). The array is populated during `buildTurnLedger` and the competitive closing.
2. **OwnerRoundLedger gains `oneOffBreakdown`** — same shape as `TurnLedger.oneOffBreakdown`; optional and absent-safe (consumers render zero or the legacy formula).
3. **Attribution sources captured during the turn** — `buildTurnLedger` accepts
   additional inputs for per-source deltas: market purchase cost, market sale
   proceeds, event-play coin effect, Community Favour exchange (coins→rep and
   rep→coins), and loan effect (repayment or bailout). The residual
   `oneOffDeltas.coins` is recomputed as `netCoinChange − incomeCoins −
   ongoingTotal − incidentCoinChange` and remains the authoritative reconciling
   figure; the breakdown entries sum to the same residual (with a small tolerance
   for rounding, documented in the model).
4. **`buildOneOffLineTooltip` renders per-source attribution** — when
   `oneOffBreakdown` is present, it lists each source with its signed amount on
   its own line (e.g. `Market purchase: −120`, `Market sale: +80`). The
   reconciliation formula remains at the bottom as a checksum line. When
   `oneOffBreakdown` is absent (legacy ledgers), the tooltip falls back to the
   existing formula-only format.
5. **All new copy is localisable** — through the existing `t()` /
   `registerLocale` system with English defaults registered at module load.
6. **Deterministic automated tests** — cover every attribution source, the
   reconciliation identity, and the absent-safe fallback; added to the existing
   tooltip suites and run through the test skill.
7. **Documentation updated** — `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   ("End-of-Turn Turn Summary Ledger and Tooltips" section) documents the new
   one-off attribution; JSDoc in `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` /
   `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` reflects the new model.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

The Turn Summary one-off row now explains itself — every market purchase, sale,
event play, Community Favour exchange, and loan effect shows its individual
contribution so the player understands exactly what drove the figure.

## Constraints

- **Must stay absent-safe.** Older ledgers without `oneOffBreakdown` render the
  legacy reconciliation formula only — no regressions.
- **Deterministic.** No new RNG consumption; every figure comes from committed
  ledger data or the engine's own per-action state.
- **One sentence of copy per source** — tooltips must remain presentational;
  no layout changes.
- **Reconciliation is authoritative.** The residual `oneOffDeltas` remains the
  ground-truth figure; breakdown entries must reconcile to it.
- **Do not invent attribution.** Where the engine has no per-source data, the
  tooltip falls back to the formula.

## Existing state

- **TurnLedger.oneOffDeltas** (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): `{ coins,
  reputation }` — computed as residual
  `netCoinChange − incomeCoins − ongoingTotal − incidentCoinChange`.
- **OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffDeltas** (optional, same shape): residual per seat.
- **buildTurnLedger** (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): accepts
  `TurnLedgerInputs` (income, ongoingCosts, incident, coins, reputation, score)
  — no per-source data flows through.
- **buildOneOffLineTooltip** (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts`):
  renders a single reconciliation formula string using `oneOffFormula` i18n key.
- **Competitive closing** (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`): mirrors the
  single-player residual formula per seat.
- **Market phase** (`src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`):
  modifies `state.resourceBank.coins` directly but does not track per-transaction
  attribution.
- **Community Favour** (`src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts`): modifies coins and
  reputation directly; no attribution tracking.
- **Event plays** (`src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`): apply coin/rep effects
  directly; event-play coin deltas are tracked in `SlotPhaseBreakdown.eventDeltas`
  but only for income-phase events, not MarketPhase event plays.
- **Loan effects** (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`):
  bank-loan repayments and bailouts modify coins during closing; no per-source
  tracking.
- **Projection model** (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`): copies
  `ledger.oneOffDeltas` into `PLProjection.oneOff`; no breakdown field.
- **Tests**: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` (612 lines,
  tooltip unit tests); `tests/main-street/turn-summary-model.test.ts` (ledger
  model tests).

## Desired change

1. **Extend `TurnLedger` and `OwnerRoundLedger`** with an optional
   `oneOffBreakdown: { label: string; coins: number; reputation: number }[]`
   field.
2. **Extend `TurnLedgerInputs`** with per-source delta fields:
   `marketPurchaseCost`, `marketSaleProceeds`, `eventPlayCoinEffect`,
   `communityFavourDelta` (signed), `loanEffect`. These are passed through from
   the closing entry points.
3. **Capture attribution in MarketPhase and loan paths** — add per-transaction
   tracking in `placeBusinessFromMarket`, `sellCard`, `resolveEvent`,
   `exchangeCommunityFavour`, and the loan repayment/bailout paths so that
   closing receives the data.
4. **Populate `oneOffBreakdown` in `buildTurnLedger`** — map per-source deltas
   to labelled entries, compute the residual, and assert the reconciliation
   identity (with documented rounding tolerance).
5. **Update `buildOneOffLineTooltip`** — render the breakdown list when present,
   followed by the reconciliation formula as a checksum.
6. **Update the competitive closing** to thread per-seat attribution data
   (reusing the same per-source tracking fields on `OwnerRoundLedger`).
7. **Add i18n keys** for each attribution source label and the checksum line.
8. **Extend tests** — model-level tests for `oneOffBreakdown` population,
   tooltip tests for every source and the fallback, and reconciliation
   assertions.
9. **Update docs** — the ledger/tooltip section in
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and JSDoc in the tooltip/projection
   modules.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnLedger`, `OwnerRoundLedger`,
  `TurnLedgerInputs` with `oneOffBreakdown` and per-source delta inputs.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — thread per-source data through
  `buildTurnLedger`; populate breakdown; handle deferred-closing and
  `finishDeferredEndOfTurn` paths.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — thread per-seat attribution into
  `OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffBreakdown`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend `PLProjection.oneOff` with
  breakdown data; pass through to tooltip builder.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — `buildOneOffLineTooltip`
  render logic, new i18n keys.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — Community Favour attribution capture.
- `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` — market purchase attribution.
- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — market sale attribution.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — event-play attribution for MarketPhase.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — loan
  effect attribution.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-model.test.ts` — model-level breakdown tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — per-source tooltip tests.

## Related work

- `MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9` — *Full breakdown in tooltips of end of turn dialog*
  (parent; this item was deferred from this work item's A3 as a follow-up).
- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — *Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger* (parent: attached
  the tooltips this item deepens).
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — *Bank Loans epic* (loan repayment/bailout attribution
  is part of this item's scope).
- `MS-0MWBZDVCH008P8X5` — *Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn
  Summary seats* (sibling deferred item; no overlap — this item adds attribution
  to the one-off row for all seats).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — Attribution granularity.** Sources are: market purchase (cost), market
  sale (proceeds), event play (coin effect), Community Favour (coins→rep or
  rep→coins, shown as a single entry with signed coin delta), and loan effects
  (repayment or bailout). If the producer wants card-level detail (which card
  name), that is a follow-up. **Recommended:** source-level labels are sufficient
  for the tooltip; card-level detail is tracked as a follow-up.
- **A2 — Rounding tolerance.** Floating-point arithmetic across multiple sources
  may produce a 1-coin rounding drift from the residual. The breakdown entries
  absorb the drift on the last entry. **Recommended:** document the tolerance in
  the model; reconcile to the residual, not to zero.
- **A3 — Competitive parity.** Competitive seats use the same per-source
  attribution as single-player. `OwnerRoundLedger.oneOffBreakdown` mirrors the
  single-player structure. **Recommended:** parity across all tabs.
- **A4 — Loan effects split.** Bank-loan repayment (negative) and bailout
  (positive, if different from repayment) are separate entries. **Recommended:**
  separate entries where both exist.

**Risks**

- **Engine mutation risk:** adding per-transaction tracking means mutating state
  during MarketPhase / closing. Mitigation: use dedicated tracking fields that do
  not affect game logic; keep them serialised (checkpoint-safe) so a save/load
  round-trip preserves the data.
- **Rounding drift:** multiple signed additions may not reconcile exactly.
  Mitigation: last-entry absorption documented in the model; assert with a
  tolerance in tests.
- **Scope creep:** the producer might want card-level detail (which specific card
  was purchased/sold). Mitigation: source-level labels only for now; card-level
  detail as a follow-up.

# Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats

## Problem statement

On a competitive closing, each seat's Turn Summary expense rows (Staff wages, Community spaces, Business costs) are category totals only: the tooltip shows the committed figure but cannot list the individual cards that make up each category, because `CompetitiveRoundLedger` / `OwnerRoundLedger` carry no per-card cost detail and `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` builds expense rows via `buildExpenseRows(seat.ongoingCosts)` which returns category-level sums.

## Users

- **Competitive players** — read the Turn Summary after each closing and need to understand exactly how each expense figure arose (which staff members, which community spaces, which businesses), so the next day's decisions are informed.

### User stories

- _As a competitive player, I want the Staff wages row to list each of my staff cards on its own line with the base cost and any modifiers (e.g. Operations Manager discount), so I can see each member's true salary._
- _As a competitive player, I want the Community spaces and Business costs rows to list each space/business on its own line with its base ongoing cost, so I can see what drove my expenses._
- _As a competitive player, I want the expense tooltips to reconcile to the committed category total, including the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction and available-coins clamp lines, so the breakdown is verifiable._

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff wages** tooltip for each competitive seat lists each of that seat's staff cards on its own line, showing the base salary (`card.ongoingCost`) and every named modifier with its signed amount (e.g. `Operations Manager: -50`), computing the member's charged salary via `computeStaffSalaryCost`, then reconciling the list to the committed category total (including the street-wide reduction and available-coins clamp lines where applicable).
2. **Community spaces** and **Business costs** tooltips list each owned space/business on its own line with its base ongoing cost (derived from the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid`), reconciling to the committed category total via the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction and clamp lines.
3. The per-card breakdown for competitive seats uses the same data sources and reconciliation as single-player: derived from the owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards` for staff and the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` for community spaces and businesses, never invented or synthesized.
4. All new copy is localisable through the existing `t()` / `registerLocale` system with English defaults registered at module load; tooltips remain **presentational** (no state mutation, no RNG), **absent-safe** (a legacy/hand-built ledger with no breakdown degrades to the committed total plus the existing explanatory note), and render the same detail level for single-player and each competitive seat's tab.
5. Deterministic automated tests cover the enhanced expense breakdowns for staff, community spaces, and businesses in competitive mode, added to the existing tooltip test suites and run through the test skill.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Hovering any expense line in the competitive Turn Summary now explains the number behind it — every staff member's base salary and discounts, every community space and business's running cost, and how each category total adds up.

## Constraints

- **Derive from committed state only.** Breakdowns are derived from `players[ownerId].staffCards` (staff) and the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` (community/business) using the same helpers single-player uses (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `getSlotOwnerId`). No engine changes.
- **Do not invent attribution.** Where the engine's per-card cost cannot be reproduced from committed state, the tooltip falls back to the committed total with an explanatory note.
- **Existing styling and interaction unchanged.** No tooltip layout, hover/tap behaviour, or `TooltipManager` styling changes.
- **No layout regression.** Multi-line tooltips must fit the existing tooltip width/wrapping; no dialog re-layout.
- **Single-player and competitive parity.** The expense breakdown detail is identical on every tab where the data exists.
- **Tests + docs required.** All tests must pass; full suite must pass.

## Existing state

- **Current competitive expense rows** — `buildExpenseRows(seat.ongoingCosts)` in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` returns `TurnSummaryExpenseRow[]` with `{ category, label, coins }` only (no `breakdown`). Called from `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` for each seat.
- **Single-player expense breakdown** — `expenseLineBreakdown(state, category)` in `MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` derives per-card detail from `state.staffCards` and `state.streetGrid`, returning `{ breakdown?: PLLineBreakdown }` with `items: PLBreakdownItem[]` and optional `streetReduction`.
- **Competitive ongoing costs** — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` in `MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` computes per-owner costs: staff from `player.staffCards` (per-player), community/business from `state.streetGrid` filtered by `getSlotOwnerId`. The `OwnerOngoingCosts` interface only carries category-level signed totals.
- **Tooltips** — `MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` already handles breakdown rendering for single-player; the same `buildExpenseLineTooltip` can render competitive breakdowns if the model threads them through.
- **Tests** — `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` has an existing test asserting competitive expense lines stay category-total only (`line.breakdown === undefined`); this test will need updating.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — new `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner(state, ownerId, category)` (or parameterised variant of `expenseLineBreakdown`), update `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` to thread breakdowns into expense rows via a per-seat `buildExpenseRowsWithBreakdown`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — no changes expected; derivation uses existing helpers (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSlotOwnerId`, etc.).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryTooltips.ts` — no changes expected; `buildExpenseLineTooltip` already handles breakdown rendering.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — add/expand tests for competitive expense breakdowns (staff per-card, community per-card, business per-card, reconciliation with Cost Cutter, absent-safe degradation).

## Related work

- `MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9` — *Full breakdown in tooltips of end of turn dialog* (parent: delivered single-player per-card expense/income/incident/totals detail; competitive expenses deferred to this item).
- `MS-0MVRNVHJ50095N9Y` — *Competitive per-seat expense category rows* (established the `OwnerOngoingCosts` category-level structure this item extends).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer may override)

- **A1 — Derive per-card detail from owner-filtered state.** Staff cards come from `players[ownerId].staffCards` (per-player, not shared `state.staffCards`). Community spaces and businesses come from `state.streetGrid` filtered by `getSlotOwnerId(state, i) === ownerId`. Uses the same helpers as single-player. **Recommended** choice — consistent with how `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` already attributes costs.
- **A2 — No engine changes.** Derivation is a pure read from committed state; no modifications to `OwnerRoundLedger`, `OwnerOngoingCosts`, or engine computation.
- **A3 — Same reconciliation as single-player.** The breakdown includes the street-wide Cost Cutter reduction as a separate line, and the total reconciles to the committed category total.

## Risks

- *Divergence risk*: re-deriving per-item figures from committed state could drift from what the engine actually deducted. Mitigation: derive only from the engine's own helpers (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, etc.) and include the reconcile-to-committed-total lines so drift is visible in the tooltip itself.
- *Regression risk*: the existing test explicitly asserts no competitive expense breakdowns; updating it must be done deliberately. Mitigation: update the assertion alongside the implementation, keep every existing behaviour.
- *Scope-creep risk*: the producer's request could pull in one-off attribution. Mitigation: explicit scope boundary — expense breakdowns only.

data.description:
**Headline:** A **Company Roster** overlay — opened by clicking the Staff Pile — lists every management-company staff member with role, salary and the exact cost of letting them go, and dismisses any one of them after a confirm step, closing the last gap where a hired staff member could not be let go from the UI.

## Problem statement

Management-company staff cannot be let go from any UI. The only lay-off path is the business Manage-Card dialog (`showSellConfirmation`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:947`), which enumerates staff with `employedAtSlot === slotIndex` — a condition management-company staff never satisfy. The GDD (D.4.2 §5) assigns their lay-off to "the company roster", which does not exist. A player who hires a €500/turn Executive therefore pays its salary for the rest of the run with no way out.

## Users

- **Main Street player (hands-on)** — hired a management-company staff member, wants it gone, and cannot find any control that does it.
  - As a player, I want to see my management-company staff in one place and let one go, so that a bad hire is recoverable.
  - As a player, I want to see what letting someone go will cost *before* I commit, so that I can weigh the salary saving against the one-off hit.
- **Main Street player (economy-focused / learning the costs)** — plans the management team around salary load.
  - As a player, I want each member's per-turn salary and the roster's total alongside the lay-off price, so that I can decide whether cutting a role pays for itself.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs the roster to be an inspectable surface for the documented lay-off rule.
  - As QA, I want the roster's rows, totals and quoted lay-off cost to match the engine's own figures, so that a change to the salary or reputation rule cannot leave the UI quoting stale numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Clicking the Staff Pile — either the card-face stack or the portrait row beneath it — opens a **Company Roster** overlay; the existing hover tooltip still works, and hand-card clicks, hand→street drags and market→hand drops around the pile and the open dialog behave exactly as they do today.
- The roster lists every management-company staff member — `state.staffCards` filtered by `!isBusinessStaffCard(card)` — exactly once, in a stable order, each row showing the member's name, its role/benefit summary, and its effective per-turn salary (resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`, never a UI-invented figure); business staff never appear.
- The roster footer states the member count and the total per-turn salary of the management team, and both update immediately when a member is let go.
- Each row offers `[ Lay off ]`, which opens a confirm step quoting the member's name, one turn's salary (coins, clamped at 0) and the reputation cost; `[ Confirm ]` executes the existing `letGoStaffCommand` through the undo manager (so the lay-off stays undoable) and `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing.
- The lay-off reputation cost becomes `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) × 100)` — the GDD's flat "1 reputation" rescaled to the shipped ×100 reputation units (€50 salary → 100, €150 → 200, €250 → 300, €500 → 500); it is applied uniformly to **every** lay-off in `letGoStaffMember()` (management-company and business staff alike), with the coin and reputation deductions both clamped at 0.
- The roster reflects state without being reopened: after a lay-off the row disappears, the footer totals change and the Staff Pile's stack/count updates; when the last member leaves, the roster shows an explicit empty state ("No management-company staff employed.") rather than an empty panel, and is suppressed entirely in `replayMode`/headless runs like every other overlay.
- Unit tests cover the roster model — membership filtering, ordering, per-row salary, footer totals, and the reputation-cost formula at its boundaries (salary 0, 50, 100, 150, 250, 500) — and the existing lay-off expectations that assert a flat −1 reputation are updated; browser/render tests cover opening from the pile click, row content, confirm/cancel, post-lay-off refresh, the empty state, and that the pile's click does not swallow hand-card input.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can finally see their whole management team in one place and let a member go — with the salary saving and the reputation hit quoted up front — instead of paying a bad hire's salary for the rest of the run.

## Constraints

- **One engine rule, one UI surface.** The only engine change is the reputation formula in `letGoStaffMember()`; no new command, no new persisted state field. The roster is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each lay-off.
- **Reuse the existing command and overlay kit.** Lay-off goes through `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable); the dialog is built from `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, following the `showStorylineJournalDialog` row-list precedent. No new overlay framework.
- **Two-type model stays authoritative.** Membership is `!isBusinessStaffCard(card)` — never a card-name list and never `employedAtSlot` re-derived inline.
- **The pile owns no roster logic.** The Staff Pile hands off a pointer-down (callback or scene method); all roster state, rows and lay-off wiring live in the roster module/overlay.
- **Quote engine figures, never re-derive them.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off coin cost and reputation cost come from the same helpers the command uses, so the confirm step cannot drift from what is actually charged.
- **No input hijack.** The pile's added click must not intercept hand-card clicks, drags or drops; assert it in the browser tests.
- **No new art.** Portraits/card faces reuse `mainStreetRenderCardSvg`.
- **Localisation.** New user-visible strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern introduced by the pile work where a key fits; overlay-only labels may follow the journal overlay's literal-string precedent.
- **Blocked by the Staff Pile.** The entry point is the pile (parent MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2, amended); implementation starts only once the pile renders and hovers.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `state.staffCards` holds every hired member. `employedAtSlot` present ⇒ business staff; absent ⇒ management-company staff. `isBusinessStaffCard()` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`) is the canonical type test.
- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) already removes the member, charges one turn's salary clamped at 0, charges a flat **1** reputation clamped at 0, and deregisters it from a business's `employedStaff` (a no-op for slotless members). `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps it in a snapshot for undo.
- The Manage-Card dialog (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:683-975`) is the only lay-off UI: it lists `employedAtSlot === slotIndex` and always acts on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]`. No management-company member ever appears.
- The Staff Pile (parent MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2) is mid-implementation: layout zone, renderer module and tooltip builder are planned children, not yet shipped. Its tooltip is management-company-only; its ACs now permit exactly one click affordance (opening this roster).
- Overlay precedent: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1655`) builds a 560-wide panel, title, row list capped at 10, "…and N earlier" overflow line, empty state, and `[ Close ]`; `s.replayMode` short-circuits before any drawing.
- Currency scale: reputation ships in ×100 units (starting reputation 200/300/500 by difficulty; discarding a card deducts its coin `cost` in reputation). The GDD's pre-scale "1 reputation" therefore reads as 100 today — this item records that rescale explicitly rather than leaving two scales in the docs.
- Tests that assert the current flat −1: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` ("1 salary + 1 reputation" — sets reputation 5, expects 4), plus lay-off calls in `tests/main-street/staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-placement-removal.browser.test.ts`.
- Docs stating the flat −1: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.2 §5) and `docs/game/card-catalog.md:620`.

## Desired change

1. **Engine (one rule).** In `letGoStaffMember()`, replace the flat −1 with `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) × 100)` where `salary` is the already-computed effective salary, clamped at 0 as today. Comment the ×100 unit and the GDD provenance.
2. **Pure roster model** (new `src/MainStreetRoster.ts`): `buildCompanyRoster(state)` → ordered rows `{ memberId, staffIndex, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation }` plus `{ count, totalSalary }`; `companyRosterIsEmpty(state)`; `layOffReputationCost(salary)` exported for reuse/tests. No Phaser imports.
3. **Roster overlay** (`showCompanyRosterDialog()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`): panel with title, one row per member (name · role/benefit · salary · `[ Lay off ]`), footer totals, `[ Close ]`, empty state; double-buffered rows rebuilt after each lay-off while the dialog stays open.
4. **Confirm step** — a small confirm dialog (or in-panel confirm state) quoting name, coin cost and reputation cost, with `[ Confirm ]` / `[ Cancel ]`, mirroring the buy-and-place premium dialog's structure.
5. **Pile hand-off** — the pile's pointer-down calls the scene's roster-open method; the pile gains no roster logic.
6. **Docs and tests** as per the acceptance criteria.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffMember()`: reputation formula becomes salary-scaled (100-unit minimum); update the doc comment.
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — **new** pure model: membership filter, ordering, per-row salary/role/let-go costs, footer totals, `layOffReputationCost()`.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — factor/shared staff summary line (role/benefit text) so the roster, the pile tooltip and `formatEmployedStaffSummary` cannot drift.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showCompanyRosterDialog()` + confirm state, modelled on `showStorylineJournalDialog()`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — **new (from parent work)**: add the pointer-down hand-off (`onOpenRoster`); no roster logic.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — wire the pile's hand-off callback through the renderer context.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showCompanyRoster()` scene entry point (journal-button precedent).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — new i18n keys/strings for the roster's tooltip/confirm copy where the bundle pattern applies.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `isBusinessStaffCard()` / `computeStaffSalaryCost()` / `getSalaryScopeSkills()` (reference; no change expected).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand()` (reference; unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.test.ts` — **new** unit tests: membership, ordering, totals, reputation-cost boundaries.
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.browser.test.ts` — **new** render tests: open from pile click, rows, confirm/cancel, post-lay-off refresh, empty state, hand input pass-through.

- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — the "lay-off costs one turn's salary plus 1 reputation" line restated.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Company Roster spec: entry point (pile click), rows, totals, confirm step, empty state, input pass-through.
- `src/README.md` — new roster module and the pile hand-off noted.

## Related work

- **MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2** — Management company staff (Staff Pile, in progress; **blocks this item**): supplies the pile whose click opens this roster. Its ACs were amended during this intake to permit exactly one click affordance.
- **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** — Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go (open, `discovered-from` this item): the Manage Card currently always lays off the most recently hired member; raised at the producer's request so both lay-off doors share one standard.
- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Staff impact (completed): the two-type staff redesign.
- **MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT** — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (completed) and **MS-0MW4MSNWR00123OZ** — Scope gate in buff aggregation (completed): the helpers that already filter management-company members.
- **MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY** — Turn summary P&L statement (completed): the nearest precedent for quoting engine-resolved per-staff costs in a UI.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** / reputation re-tune line — the reputation rescale that makes "1 reputation" read as 100 today.
- **MS-0MUMP97LQ006PP1D** — Storyline Journal overlay (completed): the row-list overlay precedent this dialog follows.
- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.2 §5, D.4.4 management-company roles and salaries), `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — a lay-off can collapse reputation outright.** With the new formula a €500/turn member costs 500 reputation, while Hard starts at 200 and Easy at 500 — firing a top-tier executive can end the run. *Mitigation:* the confirm step quotes the exact reputation charge before committing, and the roster shows the member's salary next to it; if a cap is wanted later, it is a one-line change to `layOffReputationCost()` plus a balance item, not a UI change.
- **Risk — drift between quoted and charged costs.** The confirm dialog could quote a salary the command does not charge (skill discounts, clamps). *Mitigation:* both the row and the confirm step read from the same pure model, which resolves salary through the engine helpers; a unit test pins the model's cost to `letGoStaffMember()`'s effect.
- **Risk — the pile's new click swallows hand input.** *Mitigation:* confine the hit area to the pile's own bounds and assert hand-card click/drag pass-through in the browser test.
- **Risk — the ×100 rescale leaks into docs inconsistently.** *Mitigation:* restate D.4.2 §5 and the card-catalog line in the same units in this item, and check the GDD-consistency test (`tests/main-street/gdd-staff-consistency.test.ts`) still passes.
- **Risk — scope creep into business-staff lay-off UX.** *Mitigation:* the Manage Card keeps its current selection behaviour; per-member selection there is MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11.
- **Assumption:** clicking the pile opens the roster from both the stack and the portrait row; the tooltip behaviour is unchanged.
- **Assumption:** the roster lists the acting seat's `state.staffCards` (the same source the pile renders), so competitive play shows that seat's own management team.
- **Assumption:** the roster is available whenever the pile is — no phase gating, matching the Manage Card's ungated lay-off today; it is suppressed in `replayMode`/headless runs.
- **Assumption:** row order is stable and deterministic (staff hire order, oldest first), so the overlay does not reshuffle under the player's pointer after a lay-off.
- **Assumption:** the ×100 reputation rescale is a documentation fix, not a data change: no `card-data.csv` reputation value is touched by this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How is the roster opened? — A. clicking the Staff Pile (stack or portrait row), amending the parent's 'no click action' AC; B. a separate `[ Company ]` HUD button next to Journal; C. both." **Recommended:** A — the pile is already the management-company surface and the producer had deferred its click to this item.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A. Pile click opens the roster; parent AC MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2 amended accordingly and commented.
  - Research: parent AC bullet read verbatim from `wl show`; no other overlay entry point exists for a staff surface. GDD D.4.2 §5 ("from the company roster") supports a single roster door rather than a HUD duplicate.
- Q2: "How does letting someone go work? — A. per-row `[ Lay off ]` plus a confirm dialog quoting the cost; B. per-row `[ Lay off ]` executing immediately (Manage Card behaviour); C. select a row, then one shared button." **Recommended:** A — real money plus reputation, and the roster can be long.
  - Answer (producer): "A (make reputation loss realistic amount)". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A, with the reputation amount reworked per Q4/Q5.
- Q3: "What does the roster list? — A. management-company staff only with name/role/salary/let-go cost plus count and total-salary footer; B. all staff grouped with business staff read-only; C. management-company staff only, one line each, no footer." **Recommended:** A — matches GDD D.4.2 §5 and keeps business lay-off in one place.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A.
- Q4: "What should the reputation loss be? — A. flat −1 as written; B. salary-scaled `max(1, ceil(salary/100))`; C. tier-scaled; D. salary-scaled but capped." **Recommended:** B — salary is already on the card and in the roster, so cost-to-cut is legible.
  - Answer (producer): "B but note that we have scaled reputation by 100 since the GDD was written. 1 should be 100". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: B in ×100 units — `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) × 100)`: salary 0–100 → 100, 150 → 200, 250 → 300, 400 → 400, 500 → 500.
  - Research: reputation ships in ×100 units — starting reputation 200/300/500 per difficulty (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`), and hand discard already deducts the card's coin `cost` from reputation (`src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts:178`), confirming 1 unit ≈ 100 display. Doc lines still quoted the pre-scale flat 1: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5 and `docs/game/card-catalog.md:620`.
- Q5: "Which lay-offs use the new formula? — A. all lay-offs via one rule in `letGoStaffMember()`; B. management-company only." **Recommended:** A — avoids two lay-off economies differing only by which door was used.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A. Engine change lives in `letGoStaffMember()`; the Manage Card inherits it and its flat −1 test expectation is updated.
- Q6 (producer directive, no options offered): "Raise a separate work item for laying off staff in a business."
  - Answer (producer): requested as a separate item. Source: interactive reply.
  - Result: **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** — "Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go" created with `discovered-from:MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA`.
  - Research: the Manage Card lays off `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`), so with two members employed only the newest hire can be dismissed, with no confirmation — the concrete gap the new item records.

# Layout plumbing: staffPile SLL zones and adapter/SceneLayout

## Goal

Add a `staffPile` zone to both SLL layout files and resolve it into `SceneLayout`, so the renderer can draw the Staff Pile from layout authority data instead of hard-coded pixel offsets.

## Scope

- Add a `staffPile` zone to `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — top-left anchored in the free band left of the `hand` zone (left edge of the zone is left of the hand band, `y` inside the hand band), sized for a small card-face stack plus the portrait row beneath it.
- Add the matching `staffPile` zone to `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` for tutorial parity; if the tutorial required-zone list is extended, update the expected zone-name list asserted in `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`.
- Add the pile fields (`staffPileX`, `staffPileY`, `staffPileW`, `staffPileH`, or equivalent) to the `SceneLayout` interface in `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts`, plus any presentation constants (stack offsets, portrait size, panel padding) alongside the existing hand/pile constants.
- Resolve the SLL `staffPile` zone in `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` (anchor → resolved pixel geometry at the current viewport) into the new `SceneLayout` fields.
- Extend `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` with a `staffPile` anchor contract (zone resolves to the expected pixel bounds at the 1280×720 base viewport) and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` with the tutorial `staffPile` zone composition check.

## Key files

- `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — new `staffPile` zone
- `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` — matching `staffPile` zone
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — `SceneLayout` pile fields + presentation constants
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — zone resolution into `SceneLayout`
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` — anchor contract
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` — tutorial zone composition

## Dependencies

None — pure plumbing that provides the coordinates every later child consumes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Staff Pile's position comes from a new `staffPile` zone in the SLL layout authority (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`) with a matching zone in the tutorial layout, resolved into `SceneLayout` so the pile renders to the left of the hand, against the left edge, with no hard-coded pixel offsets.
- `staffPile` exists in both layout JSON files and appears in the tutorial layout's required-zone list if that list is extended.
- `SceneLayout` exposes the new staff-pile fields and `MainStreetLayoutAdapter` populates them from the SLL anchors.
- Layout anchor tests pass, verifying the resolved `staffPile` bounds at the 1280×720 base viewport.
- The tutorial layout resolution test passes with the new zone included in the composition.

## Impact

The Staff Pile's position comes from the layout authority, so the pile lands in the free band left of the hand at the base viewport and the tutorial layout keeps the same geometry — later pile work draws against real coordinates rather than guessed pixels.

# Staff Pile renderer module

## Goal

Create `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — the module that draws the management-company staff pile: stacked card faces, count badge, portrait row, hover wiring and empty-state hiding — mirroring the `drawHandPanel()` lifecycle.

## Scope

- Create `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` as a new helper module depending only on `MainStreetRendererContext`:
  - `drawStaffPile(renderer)` — rebuilds the pile from the management-company members of `state.staffCards` on every call (destroy-then-redraw, like `drawHandPanel()`).
  - A fanned/stacked set of small card faces (oldest first, newest hire on top), each rendered with `mainStreetRenderCardSvg` at reduced size.
  - A count badge showing the number of management-company staff, drawn over the stack.
  - A small portrait row beneath the stack, one portrait per member (reusing the SVG card renderer at portrait size).
  - Hidden when the company has no management-company staff (no placeholder tile).
  - Non-interactive apart from a hover hit area confined to the pile's own bounds that shows/hides the tooltip; no `pointerdown` handlers and no lay-off control.
- Declare `drawStaffPile(): void` on `MainStreetRendererContext` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts`) and delegate it from `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` (`drawStaffPile() { drawStaffPile(this); }`).
- Call `renderer.drawStaffPile()` from `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` on the hand-refresh path, next to `renderer.drawHandPanel()`, so hires, lay-offs and `maxHandSize` changes are reflected.
- Destroy/rebuild the pile graphics per refresh so repeated refreshes do not leak game objects (same pattern as `destroyHandPanel()`).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — NEW: pile render module
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — `drawStaffPile()` declaration
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — import + delegate
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — call on the hand-refresh path
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — pile presentation constants (shared with Child 1)
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `isBusinessStaffCard()` membership test (reference only)

## Dependencies

- Child 1 (Layout plumbing) — needs the resolved `staffPile*` `SceneLayout` fields.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The pile displays only management-company staff (staff in `state.staffCards` for which `isBusinessStaffCard(card)` is false) as a fanned/stacked set of small card faces (newest hire on top), with a count badge and a small portrait row beneath the stack.
- The pile updates on every hand refresh that changes staffing (hire, lay-off, `maxHandSize` change) and is hidden when the company has no management-company staff.
- The pile is presentation-only apart from the hover tooltip: it has no click action, offers no lay-off control (deferred to the company-roster follow-up MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA), and does not intercept hand-card clicks, drags or drops.
- Hovering the stack or the portrait row shows the tooltip; leaving the pile hides it.
- `drawStaffPile()` is declared on `MainStreetRendererContext`, delegated by `MainStreetRenderer` and called on every hand-refresh cycle.
- Repeated refreshes do not accumulate stale game objects (each refresh rebuilds the pile cleanly).

## Impact

Hired management-company staff now appear on the board as a stack of card faces with a count badge and a portrait row, and hovering them explains who is on the payroll — the hire has a visible, inspectable result for the first time.

# Tooltip builder: management-company-only summary, formatter reuse, and i18n

## Goal

Create a pure tooltip content builder that produces the management-company-only summary shown when the Staff Pile is hovered, and register its strings through the existing HUD tooltip i18n tables.

## Scope

- Add a pure `buildStaffPileTooltip(state)` builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` that:
  - takes the current `MainStreetState`;
  - selects management-company staff with the canonical type test (`!isBusinessStaffCard(card)` over `state.staffCards`) — never a persisted flag or a name list;
  - returns one line per member (name, role/benefit summary, salary) plus a total count line;
  - returns `null` when there are no management-company staff, so the caller hides the tooltip.
- Reuse or extract from `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`) rather than writing a second staff-summary formatter: either call it with a management-company-only filter or extract a shared helper both the business-slot tooltip and the pile tooltip use.
- Add the new keys to `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` and their English values to `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`), following the existing bundle registration pattern; no hard-coded user-visible strings.
- Wire the builder into the pile's hover handler in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` (`s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` on enter, `.hide()` on leave).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildStaffPileTooltip()`, new i18n keys and English strings
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — reuse/extract the shared staff-summary formatter
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — hover wiring (Child 2)
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `isBusinessStaffCard()` membership test

## Dependencies

None — the builder is a pure function with no layout dependency (the hover wiring itself lands in Child 2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hovering the pile — the stack or the portrait row beneath it — shows a tooltip that lists every management-company staff member in the company with name, role/benefit summary and salary, plus the total count; the tooltip covers management-company staff only (business staff are excluded).
- `buildStaffPileTooltip(state)` returns `null` when there are no management-company staff, and a summary for one or many members otherwise.
- Staff-summary formatting is shared with `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` — no duplicated second formatter.
- New `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` entries and their `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English values are registered; no hard-coded user-visible strings.
- The compiled builder result is passed to `s.tooltipManager?.show(...)` on hover and hidden on leave.

## Impact

Hovering the Staff Pile will describe the management company — who works there, what each member does and what the team costs per turn — instead of the player having to infer it.

# Browser/render tests: placement, count badge, hover tooltip, empty state, max-capacity non-overlap

## Goal

Prove in the browser/render harness that the Staff Pile is placed by the layout authority, reflects staffing state, hides when empty and never intrudes on the hand at the widest hand the free band allows.

## Scope

- Create `tests/main-street/staff-pile.browser.test.ts`:
  - **Placement** — the pile's bounds match the `staffPile` zone resolved by `MainStreetLayoutAdapter` at 1280×720 and sit left of the hand panel.
  - **Count badge** — the badge shows the correct number for 1, several and mixed (business + management-company) rosters.
  - **Hover tooltip** — hovering the stack and hovering the portrait row both show the tooltip, whose content lists management-company staff only.
  - **Empty state** — nothing is rendered when the company has no management-company staff.
  - **Refresh** — a hire, a lay-off and a `maxHandSize` change each update the pile on the next hand refresh.
  - **Max-capacity non-overlap** — at the largest hand size whose capacity row still leaves a free band at 1280×720 (`handCenterX − maxSlots × (handCardW + HAND_SLOT_PITCH_PAD) / 2` clear of the pile's right edge), the pile's bounds do not intersect the hand panel or the capacity row. The documented bound is `maxHandSize ≤ 8` at the base viewport; the wide-hand case is covered by the overlap-budget note in the parent's Appendix.
  - **Input pass-through** — hand-card clicks and hand→street drags starting outside the pile still reach the hand cards.
- Extend `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` with the `staffPile` anchor assertions and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` with the tutorial `staffPile` composition check if Child 1 has not already added them.

## Key files

- `tests/main-street/staff-pile.browser.test.ts` — NEW: browser/render tests
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLayoutAnchors.browser.test.ts` — `staffPile` anchor contract
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` — tutorial `staffPile` composition
- `tests/main-street/hand-panel.browser.test.ts` — reference pattern for hand-panel geometry assertions

## Dependencies

- Child 1 (Layout plumbing), Child 2 (Staff Pile renderer) and Child 3 (Tooltip builder).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Automated browser/render tests cover the pile's placement, count badge, hover tooltip and empty-state hiding (with the Child 4 unit tests covering management-company selection and tooltip content), including a capacity case at the largest supported hand size.
- A capacity case at the largest hand size that leaves a free band (documented as `maxHandSize = 8` at 1280×720) asserts the pile never overlaps the hand capacity row or the hand panel.
- Hires, lay-offs and `maxHandSize` changes are each shown to update the pile on the next refresh.
- Hand-card clicks and drags outside the pile's bounds still reach the hand cards.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

The Staff Pile's behaviour is now guarded by real-scene browser tests, so a regression in its placement, count, hover summary or empty state fails the build instead of reaching players.

# Test: breakdown model detail contract

## Goal

Failing-first deterministic tests that pin the extended P&L breakdown detail the
model children add (sibling of MS-0MWBCACHZ006RTQ9), so the detail is specified
before it is implemented.

## Scope

- Extend `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-model.test.ts` (existing suite).
- Cover the fields added by the sibling model children: per-item base + named
  modifiers, per-business income items, per-item event-effect enumeration,
  incident breakdown detail, and supplementary-context derivations.
- Cover absent-safe degradation for legacy/hand-built ledgers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Model tests assert a staff breakdown item carries its base salary and each named modifier (Operations Manager discount) with signed amounts, while `coins` stays the committed contribution.
- Model tests assert each income row's breakdown exposes one item per contributing business, and the Events row additionally exposes each event effect as `name` + signed `delta`.
- Model tests assert the incident line exposes the resolved incident's committed coin/reputation deltas plus the modifiers applied to them.
- Model tests assert the supplementary context exposes day-start coins and the owning business names wherever the projection carries them.
- Model tests assert absent-safe degradation: a ledger with no `income` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown` / per-item data still yields today's line shape with no breakdown and no throw.
- The new tests are deterministic (no RNG, no clock, no Phaser) and are run through the test skill.

## Impact

The extended breakdown data is specified and locked by tests before the model
changes land, so a regression in any per-item figure fails the suite.

# Model: staff salary base and modifiers

## Goal

Let a breakdown item describe **base ± named modifiers** so a tooltip can show
how a staff member's salary was charged, while `coins` stays the committed
contribution the row already totals.

## Minimal Implementation

- `PLBreakdownItem` gains optional `base` (the unmodified per-card amount) and
  `modifiers` (`{ name, coins }[]`, signed) in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`.
- `expenseLineBreakdown` populates them for the **staff** category: `base` = the
  card's `ongoingCost` (negative, expense convention) and one modifier per
  `Operations Manager` discount, using `getSalaryScopeSkills` +
  `computeStaffSalaryDiscount` (the same helpers the engine uses).
- Community-space and business cost items carry `base` only — no invented
  modifiers.
- Invariant documented in JSDoc: `base + sum(modifiers) === coins`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PLBreakdownItem` carries optional `base` and named `modifiers`; `coins` remains the committed per-item contribution.
- Staff wage breakdown items expose `base` = the card's `ongoingCost` and a signed `Operations Manager` modifier from `computeStaffSalaryDiscount(getSalaryScopeSkills(card), card.ongoingCost)`.
- Community-space and business cost breakdown items expose a base only, with no synthesised modifiers.
- `base + sum(modifiers) === coins` holds for every emitted staff item, asserted in the sibling model tests.
- Absent-safe: an empty/absent `staffCards` or `streetGrid` still produces no breakdown rather than an empty list or a throw.
- No state mutation, no RNG, no new engine dependency: everything derives from committed state and existing engine helpers.

## Impact

A staff member's salary line can now be explained as base salary plus each
discount, without re-deriving figures in the UI.


## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — `PLBreakdownItem` base/modifiers and the staff `expenseLineBreakdown` population
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryDiscount` / `getSalaryScopeSkills` (read-only reuse)
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-pl-model.test.ts` — the assertions this child makes pass

Thread the engine's per-slot phase detail (including each event effect) into the

  reconciles.

- Each income row's breakdown enumerates one item per contributing business with that business's committed per-slot contribution (base, synergy, reputation).
- The Events income row carries each `SlotEventDelta` as a named effect with its signed delta, not only a per-business sum.

- No state mutation and no RNG; only `IncomeResult` / `SlotPhaseBreakdown` data already on the closed turn is read.

The income tooltips can now show which business and which event produced each
