data.description:
**Headline:** The business Manage Card stops laying off whichever staff member happened to be hired last: it now lists every member employed at that business, one row each with its own `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`, and an explicit confirm step quoting the exact coins and reputation before anything is charged.

## Problem statement

The Manage Card dialog is the only door for letting business staff go, but it never asks *who*: both `[ Move staff ]` and `[ Lay off ]` act on `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:926,944`). A business holding two or more members therefore exposes one control per action that silently targets the newest hire, and the lay-off executes with no cost preview and no confirmation.

## Users

- **Main Street player with a staffed business (hands-on)** — employs several specialists and wants to change the team.
  - As a player, I want to see everyone employed at this business in one place, with their effect and salary, so that I can decide which specialist is worth keeping.
  - As a player, I want to press a button that belongs to the member I mean, so that I never fire the wrong specialist by accident.
  - As a player, I want the exact coins and reputation the lay-off will charge shown before I commit, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.
- **Main Street player chasing business efficiency (economy-focused)** — compares each member's salary against its local effect.
  - As a player, I want each row's salary next to the member's effect, so that I can judge the cut by its savings.
- **Game designer / QA** — needs both lay-off doors to state one rule the same way.
  - As QA, I want the quoted cost to equal the charge that lands, so that a skill discount or a clamp cannot silently diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an **employed-staff section** with exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear. Each row shows the member's name, its role/benefit summary (from a shared formatter, not a UI-invented string) and its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- Rows are ordered deterministically (hire order, oldest first) and the panel sizes itself from the row count: at the maximum employment capacity of a business (`level + 1`) every row, button and the sell/close/cancel row are fully visible with no clipping or overlap; with no member employed the section renders nothing at all (today's empty-state behaviour).
- Each row carries `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]` addressed to **that** member. `[ Move ]` hands the member's id to `beginStaffMove`, keeping the existing `moving-staff` choreography, the 1-action cost and the per-member destination list from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` in its hover tooltip. `[ Lay off ]` opens the confirm step for that member only. Because the per-row labels are short, the section states both costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`) so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip. No control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.
- The confirm step is an overlay quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and the reputation cost from the shared `layOffReputationCost(salary)` — the single formula decided in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA and **not re-derived here**. `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand` through the undo manager (the lay-off stays undoable); `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing and returns to the member list.
- After a confirmed lay-off the dialog stays open and re-renders in place: the row disappears, the panel shrinks to fit, and once the last member leaves the staff section disappears while sell/close/cancel keep working. Rows are addressed by **member id** and resolved against `state.staffCards` at click time, so a stale row (the member is already gone, e.g. after an undo) re-renders and flashes feedback instead of acting on a shifted index.
- The activity-log entry and confirmation flash quote the charges actually applied — e.g. `Laid off <name> (−<coins> coins, −<reputation> reputation)` — replacing the hard-coded "−1 salary, −1 reputation" strings.
- Unit tests cover the pure model: membership filtering for the slot, ordering, per-row salary, coin clamp, reputation quote per row, id-addressing/staleness and the empty case; a test pins the confirm step's quoted cost to the effect of `letGoStaffMember()` (quoted == charged) including a discounted-salary member.
- Browser/render tests cover: no affordance when nobody is employed; two employed members produce two rows with two `[ Move ]` and two `[ Lay off ]` controls; the *first* row's `[ Lay off ]` lays off the *first* member (the regression this item exists for) and the *first* row's `[ Move ]` targets the first member; confirm/cancel behaviour; in-place refresh after a lay-off; the section disappearing when the last member leaves; and sell/close/cancel still working.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `src/README.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who has hired several specialists at one business can finally pick which one leaves — seeing each member's effect, salary and the exact lay-off price first — instead of a single button that always fires the newest hire.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA.** That item lands the salary-scaled reputation rule in `letGoStaffMember()` and exports `layOffReputationCost(salary)`. This item consumes that helper and the same lay-off confirm standard; the formula is not re-litigated here.
- **One confirm step, two doors.** The confirm step is being built for the roster by its child **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ**. This item reuses the shared confirm content builder and cost helpers rather than writing a second quoting implementation; if that child lands the confirm local to the roster dialog, this item factors the shared content builder out and both call it.
- **No engine change.** No new command and no new persisted state. Membership is derived from `state.staffCards` on open and after each action; lay-off stays `letGoStaffCommand` (snapshot → undoable) and relocation stays `moveStaffCommand` (1 action).
- **Address by id, never by index.** `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` is index-based, so a click resolves the row's member id to a current index at click time and refuses when the member is gone.
- **Pure model first.** Row building, salary/cost resolution and confirm copy live in a Phaser-free module so they are unit-testable; the overlay only draws.
- **One source of truth for figures.** Salaries come from `computeStaffSalaryCost`/`getSalaryScopeSkills`; the lay-off reputation cost from `layOffReputationCost`; the move destinations and 1-action cost from `buildMoveStaffAffordance`. No UI- or model-local arithmetic.
- **Overlay kit only.** `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, every element parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), suppressed in `replayMode`/headless runs. No new art — rows are text plus kit buttons.
- **Don't touch the mechanics.** Sell, close, cancel and the move/destination flow keep their current behaviour and costs; only the staff section and its confirm step change.
- **Localisation.** New user-visible strings follow the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` English-bundle pattern where a key fits; overlay-only labels may follow the journal/undo-warning literal-string precedent.
- **UK English**, no `CHANGELOG.md` edits (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The Manage Card dialog (`showSellConfirmation`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:690-975`) is a fixed 480×410 panel: card info, sale value, a close-cost line, `[ Sell ]` / `[ Close ]` / `[ Cancel ]` at `panelY + 265`, then a single `Employed here: <names>` line (`+305`) and one `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` (`+352, centerX − 110`) plus one `[ Lay off ]` (`+352, centerX + 110`).
- Both staff handlers target the newest hire: `const moveTarget = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:926`) and `const target = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` (`:944`). Neither asks for confirmation.
- Membership today: `allStaff.map((member, index) => ({ member, index })).filter(({ member }) => member.employedAtSlot === slotIndex)` (`:700-704`) — the `index` is the `state.staffCards` index `letGoStaffCommand` needs.
- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) removes the member, charges one turn's effective salary clamped at 0 and a flat **1** reputation, then deregisters it from the business's `employedStaff`. `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps it in a snapshot.
- `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) already accepts an explicit member id, resolves legal destinations through `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` and rejects illegal starts; today the dialog always passes the newest hire. `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`) accepts any employed member's id.
- Overlay precedents: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`:1655`) row list with empty state and replay short-circuit; `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog()` (`:1227`) is the confirm/cancel shape; `MainStreetLoanSelectorModel` + `MainStreetLoanOverlay` is the pure-model-plus-row-list pair; `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog()` (`:994`) the cost-quote-then-confirm structure.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders per-member `• <name> (<types>) — <description>` lines for the street tooltip — the shared role/benefit text the rows should reuse rather than re-invent.
- The Manage Card only opens for an owned, non-sold, managing-phase slot (`onSellCard` → `showSellConfirmation`), and its handlers carry defensive legality guards; nothing here changes that gating.
- Tests asserting the current behaviour: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` (lay-off with one member, expects −1 reputation and dialog dismissal; no-affordance empty case), plus `letGoStaffMember`-based expectations in `MainStreetApplicant.test.ts`, `staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` and `MainStreetIntegration.test.ts`.

## Desired change

1. **Pure model** (new `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts`, or a builder added to the roster module MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA creates): `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)` → ordered rows `{ memberId, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation, moveEnabled, moveDestinations }`, plus `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)`; reuses `layOffReputationCost`, `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `buildMoveStaffAffordance` and a shared `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` factored out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary`.
2. **Confirm content builder** (pure): `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` → title/body lines for name, coins and reputation, so the copy and arithmetic are shared with the Company Roster's confirm step rather than duplicated.
3. **Staff rows in the Manage Card** (`showSellConfirmation`): replace the single `Employed here` line and the two fixed buttons with a cost line plus a row list (name · role/benefit · salary, `[ Move ]`, `[ Lay off ]` per row), panel height computed from the row count, and an in-place re-render after a lay-off or a stale-row refusal.
4. **Confirm step**: pressing a row's `[ Lay off ]` shows the confirm overlay (confirm → `letGoStaffCommand` via the undo manager → re-render; cancel → back to the rows untouched).
5. **Copy**: log/flash strings quote the applied charges instead of the literal `−1 salary, −1 reputation`.
6. **Docs and tests** as per the acceptance criteria; the existing one-member lay-off browser test is updated to go through the confirm step.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showSellConfirmation()`: staff row list, per-row `[ Move ]`/`[ Lay off ]`, confirm step, in-place re-render, panel sizing.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — **new** pure model: slot membership, ordering, row salary/role text, coin/reputation quotes, id-addressing, confirm content.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — factor `formatStaffRoleLine(member)` out of `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` so tooltip, roster and Manage Card share one role/benefit text.
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — the module MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA creates with `layOffReputationCost()`; add the business-staff row builder here if the company roster's row shape fits (preferred), otherwise a sibling module importing the same cost helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `beginStaffMove(memberId)` from a row (reference; unchanged signature).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (reference; already per-member).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildMoveStaffAffordance` (reference) plus any new i18n keys/strings for row and confirm copy.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand` / `letGoStaffMember` (reference; formula owned by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA).
- `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` — **new** unit tests: rows, ordering, salary/cost quotes, coin clamp, stale-row handling, quoted == charged.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — extend: multiple members, per-row lay-off/move targeting, confirm/cancel, re-render, empty section, sell/close/cancel intact; update the one-member lay-off expectation.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — D.4.2 §5: lay-off from the Manage Card states member selection and the confirm step.
- `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — the shared staff-rules line (lay-off selection + cost).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Manage Card staff rows, confirm step, empty state, input behavior.
- `src/README.md` — the Manage Card staff-rows section replacing the current "press [ Lay off ]" paragraph.

## Related work

- **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** — Company roster overlay (open; **blocks this item**): lands the salary-scaled `layOffReputationCost()` in `letGoStaffMember()` and the lay-off confirm standard for management-company staff. This item applies the same rule and standard to business staff and records the follow-up (Q6) that raised it.
- **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ** — Confirm step: quote lay-off salary and reputation (blocked child of MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA): the roster's own confirm step and the shared quoted-cost surface this item's confirm must not duplicate.
- **MS-0MWC9RO0L006SYAY** — Final verification: full suite, docs consistency and pile-to-roster flow (blocked child of MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA): the roster-side verification pass; this item carries its own verification ACs.
- **MS-0MUOSULQ700186PP** — Update UI and tooltips for free re-roll and staff movement (completed): introduced the `[ Move staff ]` affordance and `buildMoveStaffAffordance`, which already takes an explicit member id — the per-row `[ Move ]` reuses it unchanged.
- **MS-0MUOSUKUC004G2VO** / **MS-0MUOSUNYR0073SI1** — staff movement engine + 1-action relocation: the command this item drives per member.
- **CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX** / **CG-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1** — job applicants and per-business employment source of truth (`employedStaff`, `employedAtSlot`).
- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Staff impact (completed): the two-type model that makes `employedAtSlot` the type test.
- **MS-0MUMP97LQ006PP1D** — Storyline Journal overlay (completed): the row-list overlay precedent.
- **MS-0MVXYCHV2000ST0C** — mid-game loan selector (completed): the pure-model + row-list-with-handlers precedent (`MainStreetLoanSelectorModel` + `MainStreetLoanOverlay`).
- Docs: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.2 §5, D.4.8), `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — the wrong member leaves anyway.** The current bug is an off-by-selection; a row UI could repeat it if it kept index-based targeting, or if the rows drifted from `state.staffCards` after an undo. *Mitigation:* rows carry member ids resolved at click time, a stale row refuses and re-renders, and a browser test asserts the first row lays off the first member under two-employee state.
- **Risk — quoted cost ≠ charged cost.** A discount, clamp or future formula change could make the confirm step lie. *Mitigation:* the quote comes from the same helpers the command uses (`computeStaffSalaryCost`, `layOffReputationCost`), and a unit test pins quote == charge for a discounted member.
- **Risk — panel growth breaks the dialog at capacity.** Six rows in a fixed 480×410 panel would overlap the sell/close buttons. *Mitigation:* height is derived from the row count and a browser test asserts no overlap at `level + 1` members.
- **Risk — scope creep back into the roster or into move mechanics.** *Mitigation:* the Company Roster's overlay stays MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA's; only the shared cost helper, role-text formatter and confirm copy are reused, and the move command/cost/phase are untouched.
- **Risk — the dialog stays open across a stale state.** Keeping it open after a lay-off is a new behaviour for this dialog. *Mitigation:* every re-render is derived from `state.staffCards`, clicks re-resolve by id, and `refreshAll()` remains the single refresh path.
- **Assumption:** the member list shows one business's employees (the managed slot), not the whole roster — the roster door is the Company Roster's job.
- **Assumption:** row order is hire order (oldest first), matching the roster's ordering decision, so rows do not reshuffle after a lay-off.
- **Assumption:** `[ Move ]` keeps its 1-action cost and its existing `moving-staff` destination-picking flow; the dialog closes on `[ Move ]` exactly as today, so no confirm step is added to relocation.
- **Assumption:** lay-off availability is unchanged (no phase or coin gate); the coin cost clamps at 0 and the reputation cost floors the run's reputation at 0, as today.
- **Assumption:** the confirm step can share its copy with the Company Roster's confirm through a pure builder even if the two overlays draw it separately — no shared rendering framework is introduced.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How does the player choose which member to let go? — A. one row per employed member in the Manage Card dialog, each with its own `[ Lay off ]` (mirrors the Company Roster); B. select a row, then one shared `[ Lay off ]` button; C. a separate lay-off picker sub-dialog." **Recommended:** A — reuses the row-list + per-row-action structure the Company Roster is standardising, so both lay-off doors look the same.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A — one row per employed member, each row owning its own `[ Lay off ]`.
  - Research: the dialog already filters exactly this set (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:700-704`); the roster's per-row `[ Lay off ]` is the AC set in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA; `showStorylineJournalDialog` (`:1655`) supplies the row-list overlay precedent.
- Q2: "The same dialog's `[ Move staff ]` button also acts on the most recently hired member. Unify? — A. leave move-staff as-is and record the divergence; B. each row gains `[ Move ]` alongside `[ Lay off ]` (per-member move selection, here); C. rows gain only `[ Lay off ]` here and per-member move selection becomes its own item." **Recommended:** C — the move path has its own `moving-staff` phase and destination picking, so folding it in doubles the scope.
  - Answer (producer): "B". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: B — each row carries `[ Move ]` and `[ Lay off ]`; per-member move selection is in scope for this item.
  - Research: the engine and controller already accept a member id (`onMoveStaffClick(staffId)`, `moveStaffCommand`, `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` whose doc comment says "the Manage-Card dialog passes the member the player chose"), so per-row `[ Move ]` needs no engine work — only the dialog's target selection changes. Far cheaper than the recommended option assumed.
- Q3: "Where does the cost-preview/confirm step live? — A. a separate small confirm dialog quoting name, coins and reputation; B. an in-panel confirm state where the pressed row's button becomes `[ Confirm ]` / `[ Cancel ]`." **Recommended:** A — one confirm component shared with the Company Roster's lay-off, so the quoted cost cannot diverge between the two doors.
  - Answer (producer): "A". Source: interactive reply.
  - Final: A — separate confirm overlay with `[ Confirm ]` / `[ Cancel ]`.
  - Research: `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1227`) and `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (`:994`) are the existing confirm-overlay precedents; MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA's roster AC sets the same confirm step for management-company members.

data.description:
**Goal:** As a player who fires a staff member, I want the reputation hit to scale with that member's salary, so that letting go of an expensive executive costs proportionally more than cutting a cheap assistant.

Part of **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (Company roster overlay). This is the item's only engine change.

## Context

- `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) currently charges the flat `1` reputation written in GDD D.4.2 §5 — but reputation ships in ×100 units (starting reputation 200/300/500 by difficulty; card discard already deducts the card's coin `cost`), so the GDD's "1" reads as **100** today.
- Salary is already computed inside the function: `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- Every existing lay-off door (Manage Card dialog, and the roster this item builds) goes through this one function, so the rule is applied uniformly (Appendix Q5, answer A).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `layOffReputationCost(salary)` is exported from the new pure module `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` and returns `max(100, ceil(salary / 100) * 100)`: salary 0 → 100, 50 → 100, 100 → 100, 150 → 200, 250 → 300, 400 → 400, 500 → 500. The module has no Phaser imports.
- `letGoStaffMember()` deducts `layOffReputationCost(salary)` instead of the flat 1, still clamping coins and reputation at 0, and its doc comment states the ×100 unit and the GDD D.4.2 §5 provenance (the GDD's pre-scale "1 reputation" = the 100 floor).
- Unit tests in a new `tests/main-street/company-roster.test.ts` pin the formula at its boundaries (0, 50, 100, 150, 250, 500) and assert that this model cost equals the reputation actually deducted by `letGoStaffMember()` for a salary-0 and a salary-≥250 member (quoted == charged).
- The existing flat −1 expectations are updated to the new figures: `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` ("1 salary + 1 reputation", sets reputation 5 → expects 4), plus the lay-off calls in `tests/main-street/staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/MainStreetIntegration.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/staff-placement-removal.browser.test.ts`. Each test is updated to assert the *new* cost (not merely relaxed), and reputation still clamps at 0.
- The site's staff-consistency expectations still pass (`tests/main-street/gdd-staff-consistency.test.ts`) — no `card-data.csv` reputation value is touched.

## Minimal implementation

- New `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` with `layOffReputationCost()` and its unit-facing doc comment; no other exports yet (the model lands in the sibling item).
- Rewrite the reputation line in `letGoStaffMember()` to call the helper; keep the existing clamp and the business `employedStaff` deregistration untouched.
- Update the four test files' expectations to the formula's values.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — new pure module, `layOffReputationCost()`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffMember()` reputation line + doc comment.
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.test.ts` — new formula/boundary tests.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — updated expectation.
- `tests/main-street/staff-skill-scope-gate.test.ts` — updated lay-off expectation.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetIntegration.test.ts` — updated lay-off expectation.
- `tests/main-street/staff-placement-removal.browser.test.ts` — updated lay-off expectation.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryCost()` / `getSalaryScopeSkills()` (reference only).

## Dependencies

None — can start immediately, independently of the Staff Pile.

## Deliverables

Engine rule, pure helper, boundary unit tests, updated existing expectations.

## Impact

Letting a staff member go now costs reputation in proportion to their salary, so letting go of an expensive executive is a heavier decision than cutting a cheap assistant.

**Goal:** As the UI author, I want one pure model that turns the game state into roster rows and totals, so that the overlay, the confirm step and the tests all quote exactly the figures the engine charges.

Part of **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (Company roster overlay).

## Context

- `state.staffCards` holds every hired member; a present `employedAtSlot` means business staff, absent means management-company staff. `isBusinessStaffCard()` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:248`) is the canonical type test — never a card-name list.
- Salaries must resolve through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`), never a UI-invented figure.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders an employed-staff line; the roster row's role/benefit summary should share one formatter so roster, pile tooltip and the existing summary cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buildCompanyRoster(state)` in `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` returns `{ rows, count, totalSalary }` where each row is `{ memberId, staffIndex, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation }`; `rows` contains exactly the management-company members (`!isBusinessStaffCard(card)`) exactly once, in staff-hire order (oldest first), and business staff never appear.
- `staffIndex` is the member's live index in `state.staffCards` (so the row can be handed to `letGoStaffCommand`), and `layOffCoins` equals the row's effective `salary` (the command charges one turn's salary, clamped at 0) while `layOffReputation` equals `layOffReputationCost(salary)` from the sibling engine item.
- `companyRosterIsEmpty(state)` reports whether the management team is empty, and `count`/`totalSalary` agree with `rows.length` and the sum of row salaries.
- The row's role/benefit summary comes from one shared formatter (extracted/refactored from `formatEmployedStaffSummary` or added beside it in `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts`) so roster row text and the existing employed-staff summary cannot diverge; no Phaser import is added to either module.
- Unit tests in `tests/main-street/company-roster.test.ts` cover: membership filtering (business staff excluded, management-company included), hire-order stability after a mid-list lay-off, per-row salary resolution with a salary-affecting skill present, footer totals, the empty case, and that `layOffCoins`/`layOffReputation` match the model's own salary and formula.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` with `buildCompanyRoster()`, `companyRosterIsEmpty()` and the row type.
- Add/reuse one role-summary formatter in `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` and use it for the row (leave `formatEmployedStaffSummary` behaviour unchanged unless a test proves otherwise).
- Write the model unit tests.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — roster model (`buildCompanyRoster`, `companyRosterIsEmpty`, row type).
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — shared role/benefit summary formatter.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `isBusinessStaffCard()`, `computeStaffSalaryCost()`, `getSalaryScopeSkills()` (reference only).
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.test.ts` — model unit tests.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the sibling engine item (settles `layOffReputationCost()` and the module).

## Deliverables

Pure roster model, shared row formatter, unit tests.

## Impact

A player can see every management-company staff member and their exact per-turn salary and lay-off cost in one list, with totals that match what the engine will charge.

**Goal:** As a player about to let someone go, I want a confirm step that quotes the exact coin and reputation cost, so that I never fire a member without seeing the price first.

Part of **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (Company roster overlay).

## Context

- Appendix Q2 (`wl show MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA`) decided: per-row `[ Lay off ]` **plus** a confirm dialog quoting the cost, because firing costs real coins and reputation.
- Mirror the existing buy-and-place premium confirm dialog's structure in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` rather than inventing a new pattern.
- The lay-off must stay undoable and must go through the existing command: `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps `letGoStaffMember()` in a snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each roster row offers `[ Lay off ]`; activating it opens a confirm step quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (the figure actually charged, clamped at 0) and the reputation cost, both read from the roster model's row for that member — never recomputed in the overlay.
- `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand(state, member.staffIndex)` through the scene's undo manager, and `[ Cancel ]` dismisses the confirm step with no state change (asserted: coins, reputation and `state.staffCards` are unchanged).
- After a confirmed lay-off the roster refreshes in place without being reopened: the fired row disappears, the footer count and total salary change, and the Staff Pile's stack/count reflect the removal; when the last member leaves the roster shows the empty state text.
- A confirmed lay-off remains undoable: after undo, the member is back in `state.staffCards`, coins and reputation are restored, and the roster shows the restored row.
- Browser/render tests in `tests/main-street/company-roster.browser.test.ts` cover the confirm text quoting model figures, `[ Cancel ]` no-op, `[ Confirm ]` lay-off with post-change row/footer assertions, the empty state after the final lay-off, and the undo restore.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `[ Lay off ]` per row and an in-panel confirm state (or a small confirm dialog) quoting name / coins / reputation.
- Wire `[ Confirm ]` to `letGoStaffCommand()` via the scene's undo manager, then rebuild the roster rows from `buildCompanyRoster()` in place.
- Extend the render tests for confirm, cancel, refresh, empty state and undo.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — per-row `[ Lay off ]`, confirm step, in-place rebuild.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand()` (reference; unchanged).
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — quoted costs (reference).
- `tests/main-street/company-roster.browser.test.ts` — confirm/cancel/refresh/undo tests.

Blocked by the roster overlay item (the confirm step lives in that dialog).

## Deliverables

Confirm step, command wiring, undo coverage, render tests.

## Impact

A player can let go any management-company staff member straight from the roster after seeing the exact coin and reputation cost up front, and can undo the decision if they change their mind.

data.description:
**Goal:** As a Main Street player with a staffed business, I want each employed member's row — its role, its benefit and its real per-turn salary, with the exact cost of letting it go — computed once in a testable module, so that what the Manage Card shows is the engine's own arithmetic and never a UI-invented figure.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- The dialog currently builds its member list inline (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:700-704`) and shows only a joined name line — no salary, no per-member cost.
- `formatEmployedStaffSummary()` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:452`) already renders `• <name> (<types>) — <description>` lines for the street tooltip; the roster model item (**MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM**) factored the per-member role line out of it. This item consumes that shared formatter (`formatStaffRoleSummary`, shipped in `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:447`) rather than re-inventing the text.
- `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) already accepts an explicit member id and resolves legal destinations through `canMoveStaffOnBusiness`.
- Employment capacity is `getEmploymentCapacity(state, slot)` = `max(1, level + 1)` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:923`); the largest shipped business `maxLevel` is 2, so the largest capacity in play today is **3**.
- **Merged test-spec child (MS-0MWCB2YH60070QEW, deleted):** the red-first plan (a test item importing the not-yet-created module) cannot pass this repo's build gate — `tsc --noEmit` type-checks `tests/`, so an import of the absent module always fails TS2307. Test-after is explicitly permitted by the implement skill, so this item delivers **both** the module and its spec tests green in one commit. The faithful red spec authored by the test-spec child is preserved at `refs/wip/MS-0MWCB2YH60070QEW` (commit `cedf3206e80ba06cb8d2a89184f97f5fb09c6f76`, file `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts`) and is **reused as the basis** — not re-authored — then fixed (its `TS7006` implicit-any errors are downstream of the missing module's `any` return and disappear once the typed module exists) and turned green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new pure module — no Phaser imports — exposes `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)`, `businessStaffIsEmpty(state, slotIndex)` and `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)`; each row carries `{ memberId, name, roleSummary, salary, layOffCoins, layOffReputation, moveEnabled, moveDestinations }`.
- `buildBusinessStaffRows` returns exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear — ordered deterministically in hire order (oldest first, i.e. `state.staffCards` order).
- Each row's role/benefit summary comes from the shared `formatStaffRoleSummary(member)` (not a UI-invented string) and its salary is its effective per-turn salary resolved through `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(member), member.ongoingCost)`.
- The row's lay-off figures come from the shared helpers only: `layOffCoins` is that salary clamped at 0 and `layOffReputation` is `layOffReputationCost(salary)` from **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA**/**MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18** — the formula decided there and **not re-derived** in this module.
- `moveEnabled` and `moveDestinations` are read from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` (1-action cost, legal destination businesses), so the row never re-derives mobility.
- `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` returns the confirm step's title and body lines quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and its reputation cost, read from the row itself — the copy and arithmetic are therefore shared with the Company Roster's confirm step rather than duplicated.
- **Spec tests land green in the same commit** (`tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts`): membership filtering for the slot (management-company staff never appear; a member of another slot is excluded), hire-order ordering, per-row salary via the engine helpers (discount applied), the coin clamp, the reputation quote per row, id-addressing and staleness (a stale row id resolves to "gone" — no index handed to `letGoStaffCommand`), the empty case (`businessStaffIsEmpty` true / `[]`), and a **quoted == charged** pin against `letGoStaffMember()` for a discounted-salary member (coins and reputation actually deducted equal the row's `layOffCoins`/`layOffReputation` and the figures in `buildLayOffConfirmContent`).

## Minimal implementation

- Factor the shared role line into one text source if not already exposed: `formatStaffRoleSummary(member)` (`src/MainStreetFormatting.ts:447`, shipped by MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM) is the shared role/benefit text; keep the tooltip's output byte-identical.
- Implement the row builder, the empty predicate and the confirm content builder in the new module, importing `layOffReputationCost`, `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `getSalaryScopeSkills` and `buildMoveStaffAffordance`.
- Add `buildLayOffConfirmContent()` beside the lay-off cost helpers so both lay-off doors (business staff and the Company Roster) can call one implementation.
- Land `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` green: start from the preserved red spec (`git show refs/wip/MS-0MWCB2YH60070QEW:tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts`), keep its structure and fixtures, and make every `it` pass against the shipped module.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — **new** pure model: slot membership, hire-order rows, salary/role text, coin clamp, reputation quote, id-addressing, confirm content.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `formatStaffRoleSummary(member)` (shipped; reference).
- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — `layOffReputationCost()` (shipped); the roster's `buildCompanyRoster` row shape is the model for the business-staff row builder.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryCost()`, `getSalaryScopeSkills()` (reference).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildMoveStaffAffordance()` (reference; Phaser-free builder, no change).
- `tests/main-street/business-staff-selection.test.ts` — **new**: the spec tests (based on the preserved red spec from the merged child).

## Dependencies

- **MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM** (roster model: shared row/role formatter) — supplies the shared `formatStaffRoleSummary` (completed).
- **MS-0MWC9P58U005ZZ18** (engine: `layOffReputationCost()`) — supplies the reputation formula this row quotes (completed).
- The deleted test-spec child **MS-0MWCB2YH60070QEW** — its deliverable is merged into this item; its red spec is preserved at `refs/wip/MS-0MWCB2YH60070QEW` and reused.

## Deliverables

Phaser-free business-staff row model, shared role-line formatter (reference), shared lay-off confirm content builder, green spec tests covering rows, ordering, salary, clamp, reputation quote, ident-and-staleness, the empty case and quoted == charged.

## Impact

The Manage Card's business staff list shows each employed member's real per-turn salary, exact lay-off cost and shared role text — figures computed once by the engine's own model, so the card can never quote an invented number.

data.description:
**Goal:** As a Main Street player with several specialists employed at one business, I want every member listed as its own row with its own `[ Move ]`, so that I can see the team, compare each salary against its effect, and relocate the member I actually mean.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- `showSellConfirmation()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:690-975`) is a fixed 480×410 panel (480×360 when nobody is employed): card info, sale value, close-cost line, `[ Sell ]`/`[ Close ]`/`[ Cancel ]` at `panelY + 265`, then a single `Employed here: <names>` line at `+305` and one `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` at `+352, centerX − 110`.
- The move handler targets `employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]` today (`:926`), i.e. the newest hire, whatever the player clicked.
- The engine and controller already accept a member id: `s.beginStaffMove(memberId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts:1088`) → `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:362`), which drives `moveStaffCommand` (exactly 1 action). The affordance builder `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId?)` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:613`) resolves that member's legal destinations — no engine change is needed.
- Overlay precedent for a row list: `showStorylineJournalDialog()` (`:1655`); the overlay kit is `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` / `dismissOverlay`, depths 199/200/201, all objects tracked in `s.overlayObjects` and parented into `s.hudContainer`, suppressed in `replayMode`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Manage Card dialog renders an employed-staff section of exactly one row per member employed at that slot (`employedAtSlot === slotIndex`) and nothing else — management-company staff never appear — each row showing the member's name, its role/benefit summary from the shared formatter and its effective per-turn salary, with its own `[ Move ]`.
- Rows are ordered deterministically in hire order (oldest first) and the panel sizes itself from the row count: with no member employed the section renders nothing at all (today's empty-state behaviour); with two members employed two rows and two `[ Move ]` controls render; at a business's maximum employment capacity (`level + 1`, 3 today) every row, every button and the sell/close/cancel row are fully visible with no clipping or overlap.
- `[ Move ]` hands that row's member id to `beginStaffMove`, keeping the existing `moving-staff` choreography and the 1-action cost, and the per-member destination list from `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, member.id)` in its hover tooltip; no control in the dialog acts on "the most recently hired" member implicitly.
- The section states both affordance costs once in its own line (`Move: 1 action · Lay off: 1 turn's salary + reputation`), so neither cost is hidden behind a tooltip.
- Browser/render tests in `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` cover: no staff section when nobody is employed; two employed members producing two rows with two `[ Move ]` controls; the *first* row's `[ Move ]` targeting the *first* member; the capacity layout with no overlap; and `[ Sell ]`, `[ Close ]` and `[ Cancel ]` still working with the rows present.

## Minimal implementation

- Replace the `Employed here: …` line and the single `[ Move staff (1 action) ]` button with a cost line plus one row per `buildBusinessStaffRows(state, slotIndex)` entry, laid out from a row height constant.
- Derive `panelH` from the row count (plus the fixed sell/close/cancel block) instead of the current 360/410 pair; keep every element parented and tracked exactly as today.
- Per row, create `[ Move ]` and bind its `pointerover`/`pointerout` to `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, row.memberId).tooltip` and its `pointerdown` to `dismissOverlay(...)` + `s.beginStaffMove(row.memberId)`.
- Keep the row section's teardown/rebuild in one helper so the lay-off item can re-render in place from the same code path.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showSellConfirmation()`: staff row list, per-row `[ Move ]`, cost line, panel height from row count.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — `buildBusinessStaffRows()` / `businessStaffIsEmpty()` (sibling model item).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `beginStaffMove(memberId)` (reference; unchanged signature).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onMoveStaffClick(staffId)` (reference; already per-member).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildMoveStaffAffordance(state, staffId)` (reference) plus any new tooltip/row strings under the `HUD_TOOLTIP_I18N_KEYS` / `HUD_TOOLTIP_STRINGS` pattern.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rows, per-row move targeting, empty section, capacity layout, sell/close/cancel intact.

## Dependencies

- The model item (sibling child) — supplies `buildBusinessStaffRows()` and the shared role line.
- **MS-0MUOSULQ700186PP** (completed) — supplied `buildMoveStaffAffordance` / `[ Move staff ]`; this item only changes the target selection.

## Deliverables

Row-per-member staff section with per-row `[ Move ]`, hire-order layout, row-count-driven panel height, capacity-safe rendering, render tests.
## Impact

The Manage Card now lists every employed specialist as its own row with its own [ Move ], so the player can see the whole team, compare each salary, and relocate the exact member they mean instead of always the newest hire.

data.description:
**Goal:** As a Main Street player about to fire a specialist, I want to press the `[ Lay off ]` that belongs to the member I mean and see the exact coins and reputation first, so that a €500/turn executive cannot end my run unannounced.

Part of **MS-0MWC952QU000HQ11** (Business staff lay-off: choose which employed member to let go).

## Context

- The lay-off handler currently targets the newest hire (`const target = employedStaff[employedStaff.length - 1]`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:944`), executes immediately, dismisses the dialog and logs the literal `Laid off <name> (−1 salary, −1 reputation)`.
- `letGoStaffCommand()` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:903`) wraps `letGoStaffMember()` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1513`) in a snapshot, so the lay-off is undoable: coins, reputation and the member all come back. The reputation rule itself belongs to **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (`layOffReputationCost(salary)`) and is only quoted here.
- Confirm-overlay precedents: `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog()` (`:1227`) and `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog()` (`:994`); instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), suppressed in `replayMode`.
- The Company Roster's own confirm step is **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ**; this item must not ship a second quoting implementation — the shared `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` from the model item is the single source and, if that child rendered its confirm copy locally, this slice swaps it onto the shared builder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each row's `[ Lay off ]` opens the confirm step for that member only, quoting the member's name, one turn's salary in coins (clamped at 0) and the reputation cost from the shared `layOffReputationCost(salary)` — the single formula decided in MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA and **not re-derived here**.
- `[ Confirm ]` executes `letGoStaffCommand` through the scene's undo manager, so the lay-off stays undoable (after undo the member, coins and reputation are restored), and `[ Cancel ]` changes nothing (coins, reputation and `state.staffCards` unchanged) and returns to the member list.
- After a confirmed lay-off the dialog stays open and re-renders in place: the row disappears and the panel shrinks to fit, and once the last member leaves the staff section disappears while `[ Sell ]`, `[ Close ]` and `[ Cancel ]` keep working.
- Rows are addressed by **member id** and resolved against `state.staffCards` at click time, so a stale row (the member is already gone, e.g. after an undo) re-renders and flashes feedback instead of acting on a shifted index.
- The activity-log entry and confirmation flash quote the charges actually applied — e.g. `Laid off <name> (−<coins> coins, −<reputation> reputation)` — replacing the hard-coded `−1 salary, −1 reputation` strings.
- Browser/render tests cover two employed members producing two rows with two `[ Lay off ]` controls, the *first* row's `[ Lay off ]` laying off the *first* member (the regression this item exists for), confirm and cancel behaviour, the in-place refresh after a lay-off, and the section disappearing when the last member leaves; the existing one-member lay-off test is updated to go through the confirm step.

## Minimal implementation

- Bind each row's `[ Lay off ]` to open the confirm overlay built from `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)`, keeping the row list beneath it.
- On `[ Confirm ]`: re-resolve the row's member id to a current `state.staffCards` index; refuse with feedback when the member is gone; otherwise execute `letGoStaffCommand(state, index)` through `s.undoManager`, log/flash the applied figures, then rebuild the row section in place and `s.refreshAll()` + `s.refreshUndoRedoButtons(...)`.
- On `[ Cancel ]`: dismiss only the confirm layer and return to the rows untouched.
- Point the Company Roster's confirm step at the same `buildLayOffConfirmContent()` if it duplicated the copy.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — per-row `[ Lay off ]`, confirm overlay, id→index resolution, in-place rebuild, panel resize.
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` — `buildLayOffConfirmContent(row)` and the row's `layOffCoins` / `layOffReputation` (model item).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffCommand()` (reference; unchanged).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `letGoStaffMember()` / `layOffReputationCost()` (reference; formula owned by MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRoster.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — the Company Roster's confirm step (MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ) if it needs re-pointing at the shared builder.
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — multi-member lay-off targeting, confirm/cancel, refresh, empty section.

## Dependencies

- The rows/`[ Move ]` slice (sibling child) — supplies the row section and its rebuild helper.
- **MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA** (parent blocker) — the salary-scaled `layOffReputationCost()` and the lay-off confirm standard this step follows.
- **MS-0MWC9PCSB001MCMQ** (Company Roster confirm step) — the other door sharing the same confirm content; this item unifies the copy with it.

## Deliverables

Per-row `[ Lay off ]` with a quoted confirm step, undoable execution, in-place refresh, stale-row safety, applied-charge log and flash, render tests.


## Impact

A player can lay off exactly the member they mean from the Manage Card after seeing the exact coin and reputation cost up front, and the dialog re-renders in place with the panel shrinking as members leave.

- `CHANGELOG.md` is managed by the release pipeline — do not edit it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the README, and the relevant docs site entries: `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` D.4.2 §5 (lay-off from the Manage Card now states per-member selection and the confirm step), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (the shared staff-rules line: lay-off selection plus cost), `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (Manage Card staff rows, per-row `[ Move ]`/`[ Lay off ]`, the confirm step, the empty state and the input behaviour) and `src/README.md` (the Manage Card staff-rows section replacing the current "press [ Lay off ]" paragraph).

## Minimal implementation

## Key Files

# Staff go to business or management company

## Problem statement

Hiring a **business staff** card (e.g. the Delivery Driver, `staff-delivery`) from the general market row does not set `employedAtSlot`, so the two-type model's runtime test (`isBusinessStaffCard` = "has an `employedAtSlot`") classifies the member as **management-company staff**. The member then appears in the management-company roster and Staff Pile, its business-scope effect is inert, its salary is still charged, and there is no way to correct it — the roster offers only *Lay off*, never *Assign to a business*. The player reported exactly this: a hired Delivery Driver "went to the management company" even though its card type is *Business*, and clicking it offered no way to assign it to an appropriate business.

**Chosen model (producer decisions Q1/Q2/Q3).** Business-staff cards are hired **unassigned** into the player's staff pool (the Staff Pile) — there is **no** hire-time destination step; the member receives no business-scope benefits until it is employed, while its salary costs remain. The player assigns an unassigned business-staff member to a business afterwards by clicking it / its roster row (*Assign to business*). The docs that currently promise hire-time placement are updated to describe this assign-later model. Roster and Staff-Pile classification is corrected so unassigned business staff are never shown as management-company staff, and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff so balance runs stop silently wasting hires.

## Users

- **Human player (single-player)** — hires a business-staff card from the market row; the member joins the staff pool unassigned and is assigned by the player via the staff surface.
  - As a player, when I hire a Delivery Driver I want to click it afterwards and assign it to one of my Food/Commerce businesses, so that its adjacency purchase discount actually applies.
  - As a player, when an unassigned business-staff member has no matching business yet, I want to see it labelled as *unassigned business staff* (not management company), with costs and benefits behaving accordingly, so I know I must either build a matching business or lay the member off.
- **Human player (competitive)** — the same flow, restricted to the businesses their seat owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business-staff hire is unchanged and unassigned is first-class. Hiring a business-staff card (`staffCardScope(card) === 'business'`) from the general market row joins the player's staff pool with **no** `employedAtSlot` and **no** hire-time destination step (Q1-B). An unassigned business-staff member receives no business-scope benefits while its salary is still charged (Q2-B); management-company staff hire is unchanged.
- *Assign to business* affordance. From the staff-management surface (the roster overlay opened from the Staff Pile / a member click), an unassigned business-staff member offers an *Assign to business* action; the player picks a destination that satisfies the existing placement predicate (`canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`: business-type match via `staffMatchesBusiness`, free employment slot via `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, competitive ownership via `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). The assignment is executed through `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` — initial placement of an unassigned member stays action-free, a later move of an employed member stays 1 action — and is undoable and logged.
- No legal destination is handled gracefully. When no business the acting seat may employ at matches the member's `allowedBusinessTypes` with a free slot, the member simply remains unassigned (Q2-B): the assign action reports the reason (e.g. "no matching business with a free employment slot") and spends nothing; the member keeps appearing as unassigned business staff until a legal destination exists or it is laid off.
- Roster and type surfaces classify by card type (Q3-A). The management-company roster and Staff Pile list management-company staff only; unassigned business staff are surfaced as an explicit *unassigned business staff* group with the assign affordance and are never presented as management-company staff; employed business staff appear on their business (Manage Card) as today. Effect semantics keyed on `employedAtSlot` are unchanged.
- Lay-off stays available for unassigned business staff. Dismissal of an unassigned business-staff member works from the staff surface with the same quoted cost (one turn's salary + the salary-scaled reputation cost) as other doors.
- Single-player AI / Monte-Carlo hires place business staff (Q3-A). In AI-driven play (Monte Carlo / auto-play), a business-staff hire places the member at a legal destination business as part of the hire; when no legal destination exists the hire action is not taken, so an AI hire is never silently inert. The competitive AI remains staff-free (unchanged).
- Deterministic automated tests cover the matrix: business-staff hire → unassigned for the human player; the assign affordance's legality matrix (type match / no match / no free slot / opponent-owned destination in competitive / no owned business at all); assign is action-free on initial placement and 1 action on relocation; undo/redo and save/load round-trips; roster and Staff-Pile classification (management-company vs unassigned business staff); AI hire-and-place and AI skip-when-no-destination; management-company hire unchanged — seeded and run through the test skill.
- Documentation updated (Q1-B: "update GDD if necessary"). The hire-flow wording in `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4) is updated to the assign-later model (currently they promise "hiring business staff chooses the destination business"); code comments, JSDoc, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries are updated too.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who hires a business-staff card (such as the Delivery Driver) can click the member afterwards and assign it to the business it works at, so the hire actually does what the card promises — until then it is honestly labelled *unassigned business staff* with its costs, rather than masquerading as a management-company employee.

## Constraints

- **One placement predicate.** Destination legality must reuse `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (and therefore `staffMatchesBusiness`, `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). Do not add a second business-type or ownership check.
- **No hire-time placement step.** Per Q1-B the market-row hire flow is unchanged; the fix is the assign affordance and the classification/doc corrections, not a `placing-staff` phase at hire.
- **Effect semantics stay keyed on `employedAtSlot`.** An unassigned business-staff member's business-scope skills remain inert (the existing scope gate); classification changes affect *display surfaces and AI behaviour*, not buff resolution.
- **Action economy unchanged.** Hire is 1 action; assigning an unassigned member (initial placement) is free; relocating an employed member stays 1 action (`isStaffRelocation`); management-company staff are never placed or relocated.
- **Determinism preserved.** AI/enumeration and applicant-resolution changes must not add or reorder `state.rng` draws in a way that changes seeded outcomes (Monte Carlo baselines may shift only as the intended Q3-A consequence, and must stay seeded/deterministic).
- **Single-player untouched where it should be.** The competitive ownership gate stays a no-op without `ownerTaggedGrid`; existing single-player behaviour passes.
- **No new scope.** Staff salaries, the two-type effect model, the applicant flow and the AI's staff-free competitive strategy are unchanged; extra opportunities (e.g. rebalancing staff salaries) are recorded as linked work items, not folded in here.
- **Backward-compatible saves.** Loads must tolerate older saves that contain unassigned business staff.

## Existing state

- **Hire path never places.** `purchaseStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1061`) deducts coins, removes the row card and pushes `{ ...card }` into `state.staffCards` (`:1085`) with **no** `employedAtSlot`; `hireStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:904`) simply delegates to it. `canPurchaseStaff` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1043`) only checks presence and coins — never business availability (this is now the chosen behaviour for the player, per Q2-B).
- **UI hires immediately.** `onStaffCardClick` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:785`) validates with `canPurchaseStaff` and executes `hireStaffCardCommand` (`:827`) with no destination step — retained as-is under Q1-B.
- **The engine already knows the card is business staff.** `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:996`) gates on `staffCardScope(member) === 'management-company'` (`:1014`), and `staffCardScope` (`src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts:147`) falls back to the template marker for an unplaced card — so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *business* staff to the engine, and `placeStaffOnBusiness` can already place it.
- **The roster uses a different test.** `isBusinessStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:248`) is `employedAtSlot !== undefined`, so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *management-company* staff to every roster/tooltip surface: `buildCompanyRoster` (`src/MainStreetRoster.ts:93`), `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:262`) and `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:701`). That is the visible contradiction ("listed as a business staff member" but sitting in the management company).
- **Effects are inert, salary is not.** Business-scope buffs resolve from `business.employedStaff` (`src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`), so an unplaced member contributes nothing, while `applyStaffOngoingCosts` still charges its salary — the behaviour the producer confirmed as intended (Q2-B).
- **No assign door today.** `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1906`) offers only [Confirm lay-off]; business rows appear only in the Manage Card once the member is already employed (`buildBusinessStaffRows`, `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`); `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1091`) rejects an unplaced member (`employedAtSlot == null`) and `buildMoveStaffAffordance` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:632`) therefore never offers it. `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:922`) is the correct action-free initial-placement command but has **no live UI caller**.
- **Docs promise the superseded model.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:509` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md:544` state that hiring business staff "also chooses the destination business — its initial placement is free and part of the hire action"; under Q1-B this wording is updated to the assign-later model (in scope).
- **Single-player AI hires without placing.** `enumerateLegalActions` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:837-860`) offers `hire-staff` for any affordable, not-already-employed staff card, with no placement step, so a Monte-Carlo AI hire of business staff is inert (Q3-A fixes this).
- **Tests.** `tests/main-street/staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts` asserts that hiring *management-company* staff never assigns a destination; `staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts` covers the coin/hand mechanics only; no test covers the assign-affordance flow or roster classification of unassigned business staff.

## Desired change

1. Keep the market-row hire exactly as it is (Q1-B): business staff join unassigned; no destination step.
2. Add the *Assign to business* interaction for unassigned business-staff members: an affordance on the staff surface (roster overlay / member click), a destination picker derived from `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`, executed via `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (action-free initial placement), undoable and logged.
3. Correct the classification surfaces (Q3-A): `buildCompanyRoster`, `selectManagementCompanyStaff`-driven displays and `buildStaffPileTooltip` must not present business-staff members as management-company staff; an explicit *unassigned business staff* group/row with the assign affordance (and lay-off) is added.
4. Align the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path (Q3-A): business-staff hires place the member at a legal destination as part of the hire, or the hire is skipped when none exists.
5. Update the rules/GDD/catalogue docs to the assign-later model (Q1-B "update GDD if necessary").
6. Cover the matrix with deterministic tests; keep saves backward compatible (unassigned members load unchanged and remain assignable — no silent place/delete/reclassify).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — `buildCompanyRoster` (`:93`) classifies by `staffCardScope`; an *unassigned business staff* group with assign affordance data (reuse the `buildMoveStaffAffordance`-style destination derivation, but accepting unplaced members).
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — display classification for unassigned members; `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`:262`) / `isBusinessStaffCard` (`:248`) usage split between display and effects.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`:1906`) gains an *unassigned business staff* section with [ Assign to business ] (and [ Lay off ]); the assign destination picker flow.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`:701`) excludes unassigned business staff; an assign affordance builder (`buildAssignStaffAffordance`) listing legal destinations for an unplaced member.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — assign flow wiring (destination-pick phase or reuse of `moving-staff` with an accept-unplaced predicate); `onMoveStaffClick` (`:362`) / `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1091`) boundary.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`:922`) is the assignment command (may need an unplaced-member legality path; `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` already accepts one).
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `enumerateLegalActions` (`:837`) hire-staff for business staff carries/requires a legal destination slot (hire-and-place composite), skipped when none; `executeAction` handling.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — any legality tweaks to expose the assign action and confirm `placeStaffOnBusiness` handles the unplaced member (it already does via `staffCardScope`).
- `tests/main-street/staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts`, `staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts`, `staff-placement-commands.test.ts`, `company-roster.test.ts`, `staff-pile.test.ts`, `staff-movement.test.ts`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`-based fixtures — new assign-flow, classification, save/load and AI hire-and-place coverage.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — hire-flow wording updated to the assign-later model.

## Related work

- `MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB` — *Implement two-type staff redesign deltas in card data and engine* (introduced the business/management-company split and the `staffCardScope` marker).
- `MS-0MW4MSNMJ006E9JH` — *add skill scope classification and type-consistent assignment* (the scope gate that makes an unassigned business-staff skill inert).
- `MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA` — *Company roster overlay: view and lay off management-company staff* (the roster this member wrongly appears in; the surface gaining the assign affordance).
- `MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM` / `MS-0MWCB35QG0030XU6` — *Roster model* / *Manage Card: staff rows and per-row move* (the row/move patterns to reuse).
- `MS-0MWBB146L005SU31` — *Player hired staff, staff went to AI business* (the sibling ownership bug in the same hire/placement area; established the save-repair precedent and the ownership predicate).
- `MS-0MUOSUKUC004G2VO` / `MS-0MUOSUNYR0073SI1` — *staff movement* / *gate relocation with 1 action* (`placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` and `isStaffRelocation`).
- `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND` — *Staff effects are not implemented* (open; the inert-effect symptom overlaps but is a separate defect).
- Earlier staff-placement work: `MS-0MU3BTSQ8006ZRCU` (placement engine/commands), `MS-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1` (per-business `allowedBusinessTypes` / `employedStaff`), `CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ` (specialization applicants), `CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX` (walk-on applicant flow).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer confirmed)

- **D1 — Q1 answered (b): post-hire *Assign to business* affordance only.** No hire-time destination picker; the market-row hire flow is unchanged (member joins unassigned). The GDD/core-rules/catalogue wording that currently promises hire-time placement is updated to the assign-later model (in scope, per the producer's "update GDD if necessary"). The producer's phrase "hire goes to the hand" is read as *joins the staff pool / Staff Pile*: staff cards are never moved to the card hand by engine design (`moveToHand` rejects staff, CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55) — if the producer intended the card hand instead, that is a much larger scope change and should be raised at planning.
- **D2 — Q2 answered (b): hire proceeds unassigned, benefits not received, costs remain.** When a business-staff hire has no legal destination, the hire is not refused; the member stays unassigned, its business-scope effects are inert, and its salary is still charged. The assign action surfaces the reason and spends nothing.
- **D3 — Q3 answered (a): both.** Roster/Staff-Pile classification is corrected (unassigned business staff shown as *unassigned business staff*, never management-company), and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff at a legal destination or skips the hire (competitive AI stays staff-free).
- **A4 — No silent save repair.** Unlike the competitive cross-seat repair (`MS-0MWBCX7MS00960BH`), an unassigned business-staff member is *not* silently placed on load — the player assigns it (or it stays unassigned until they do).
- **A5 — Scope is classification + assign UI + AI hire placement + docs.** No salary, effect-strength, tier or card-data changes; any such opportunity is a linked follow-up item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix shape): How should a business-staff hire get onto a business?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(b) — post-hire *Assign to business* affordance only (hire unassigned, assign later); update GDD if necessary." Decision recorded as **D1**. Interpretation note: the producer's follow-up "hire goes to the hand" is treated as *the staff pool / Staff Pile*, because staff cards are never moved to the card hand by engine design (`moveToHand` rejects staff, CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55; `staff-general-market-state.test.ts`). If the producer intended the card hand, that must be raised at planning as a scope change.
- **Q2 (no legal destination): When a business-staff hire has no matching business with a free slot, what should happen?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(b) — the hire goes through as unassigned; benefits are not received (effects inert until employed) and costs remain (salary charged)." Decision recorded as **D2**.
- **Q3 (scope): Should the fix also correct roster classification and align the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(a) — both: roster classification correction and single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire alignment." Decision recorded as **D3**.
- **Q: Which hire path produced the reported Delivery Driver?** — Answer (agent, evidence): the general market row (`onStaffCardClick` → `hireStaffCardCommand` → `hireStaffCard` → `purchaseStaffCard`), which is the only non-applicant hire path and never assigns `employedAtSlot`. The walk-on applicant path does place business staff (`hireStaffApplicant` sets `employedAtSlot = pending.targetSlotIndex`). Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Is the Delivery Driver business staff or management-company staff?** — Answer (agent, evidence): business staff. `src/card-data.csv` ships `handSlotsAdded` and `actionsPerTurn` empty and `allowedBusinessTypes = Food|Commerce`, so `staffCardScope` returns `'business'`; `docs/game/card-catalog.md` classifies its Type as `Business`. The runtime only *downgrades* it to management-company because `employedAtSlot` is absent. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Why does clicking the member offer no assignment?** — Answer (agent, evidence): the Company Roster row (`showCompanyRosterDialog`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1906`) renders only a lay-off button, and the relocation affordance (`buildMoveStaffAffordance` → `canMoveStaffOnBusiness`) rejects a member with `employedAtSlot == null`. `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` exists but has no UI caller. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Do the docs currently promise hire-time placement?** — Answer (agent, evidence): yes — `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:509` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md:544` both state that hiring business staff chooses the destination business as part of the free initial placement; under Q1-B this wording is updated to the assign-later model (in scope). Source: repo inspection.

# Intake brief: Move management company staff roster (MS-0MWE6AULW004EATJ)

## Problem statement

The management-company **Staff Pile** currently renders at the bottom-left of the screen (SLL `staffPile` zone at x: 0.016, y: 0.785, w: 0.172, h: 0.142). The producer wants it relocated to the **bottom-right**, using the space in the right column **above the End Turn button row** — a purely positional/visual change; the pile's behaviour (hover tooltip, click-to-open Company Roster) is unchanged.

## Users

- **The player** — sees the management-company staff pile in a new position; benefit is a cleaner, better-balanced screen layout (nothing claimed beyond positioning).
- User story: "As a player, I see the management-company staff pile at the bottom right of the screen, above the End Turn button row, so the bottom-left corner is freed up and the layout feels balanced."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The management-company Staff Pile renders in the **bottom-right** column of the screen, positioned **above the End Turn button row** (the SLL `staffPile` zone is relocated accordingly; both the base `main-street.layout.json` and the tutorial `main-street-tutorial.layout.json` stay in sync).
- The pile **fits within the available space**; a full card face is **not** required — a compact representation (smaller stack/portraits, count badge) is acceptable, and nothing overlaps the incident queue, challenge panel, End Turn / action buttons, or hand capacity row.
- The pile's existing interactions are preserved: hover shows the management-company-only summary tooltip, and pointer-down hands off to open the Company Roster (replay mode still shows no affordances).
- The empty state is preserved: no management-company staff ⇒ nothing is rendered (no placeholder tile).
- Layout/hit-area logic (`staffPileHitBounds`) is updated for the new right-side position — the current "clamp to the free band left of the hand" logic no longer applies unchanged — and hand-card input, market→hand drops and hand→street drags remain untouched.
- All affected unit/browser tests (layout anchors, staff-pile renderer, company-roster hand-off, tutorial layout resolution, geometry helper) are updated to the new position and pass; the full project test suite passes with the changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Impact

**User-facing:** the management-company staff pile now lives at the bottom right of the screen above the End Turn button, freeing the bottom-left corner and balancing the layout — with no change to how it is used.

## Constraints

- **No overlap** with incident queue, challenge panel, End Turn/action row buttons, or the hand capacity row (producer: "No" impact on those components).
- **Compact fit allowed** — the full card face is not required (producer answer 4); only position changes, not behaviour.
- **Tutorial layout must stay in sync** — `main-street-tutorial.layout.json` mirrors the staffPile zone; the tutorial layout may also need its highlight zone / collision-warning handling adjusted (`MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`, `tutorialLayoutIssues.ts`).
- The pile remains **derived, never persisted**, rebuilt from `state.staffCards` on every hand refresh, and drawn **behind** the hand layer (depth ordering preserved).

## Existing state

- `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — `staffPile` zone at x: 0.015625, y: 0.784722, w: 0.171875, h: 0.141667 (bottom-left).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — draws a fanned card stack + count badge + portrait row + hover hit area; contract MS-0MWBWKZ1G006IBH2.
- `staffPileHitBounds` clamps the hit area to the free band **left of the hand capacity row** — the hand sits at the bottom of the screen, so the clamp logic is tied to the old left-side position.
- `STAFF_PILE_DEPTH` sits below the hand panel — needs review because the pile now sits on the right, away from the hand.

## Desired change

Relocate the `staffPile` SLL zone to the bottom-right column above the End Turn button row; update the renderer (compact fit allowed), the hit-area clamping logic, the tutorial layout mirror + highlight/collision handling, and all affected tests. No engine/model change — this is presentation only.

## Key Files

- `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — relocate the `staffPile` zone rect to the bottom-right, above the End Turn button.
- `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` — mirror the relocated `staffPile` zone (tutorial layout stays in sync).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — staffPile zone resolution feeding `staffPileX/Y/W/H` layout fields (verify no changes needed beyond the JSON).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStaffPile.ts` — compact rendering and reworked hit-area clamping for the right-side position.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — `STAFF_PILE_*` size constants (may need adjustment for the tighter space).
